title: Beginning Watercolor Class

description:
Discover the joy of Watercolor Painting!

Unlock your creativity with our Beginning Watercolor Class, designed for beginners and advanced beginners alike! Dive into the vibrant world of watercolor and master the techniques to create stunning artwork.





Course Details:

  * Instructor: Eva Mautner

  * Practice layering color with a grid exercise
  * Proper brush care and maintenance
  * Learn to correct mistakes and know when to leave them

Key Skills You'll Gain:

  * Layering and drying techniques

title: SUP Yoga on the Petaluma River
location: The Floathouse Petaluma, 50 Water Street, Petaluma, CA
description:
This is SUP Yoga the Petaluma way—right downtown, deeply local, and rooted in our river. 
SUP Yoga at The Floathouse Petaluma invites locals to slow down and experience the Petaluma River as part of everyday life. Though we launch from the heart of downtown, the central turning basin holds a special calm. Once you’re on the water, the noise drops away and the river becomes what many of us love most about Petaluma: peaceful, welcoming, and shared. 
Sessions are gentle and all-levels, designed for neighbors as much as newcomers. We begin with a short, easy paddle from the docks to get comfortable on your board (knees are always welcome), then anchor together so tidal movement won’t interrupt your flow. From there, you’re free to move, stretch, breathe, rest—or simply float—guided by expert instruction and supported by community. 
Morning sessions (9:30–11:00 am) are a beautiful way to start the day—flow first, then roll into coffee, brunch, errands, or a riverside walk. Friday evening sessions ease you into the weekend, offering a chance to unwind on the water before heading out for dinner, music, or a sunset stroll downtown. 
All equipment is provided, including wide, ultra-stable paddleboards. No prior yoga or paddleboarding experience is needed—just curiosity and a willingness to try something new. 
If you’ve ever walked past the docks and wondered what it’s like out there, this is your invitation. It’s YOUR river. Come out and play.

title: Napa County Historical Society Announces the   2026 Heritage Halloween Tulocay Cemetery Tour
description: Heritage Halloween Tulocay Cemetery Tour Step into Napa’s past during the 2026 Heritage Halloween Tulocay Cemetery Tour, presented by the Napa County Historical Society and sponsored by Napa County Landmarks. Founded in 1857 on the Juarez Tulucay Rancho, Tulocay Cemetery is among the oldest public cemeteries in California and has served the Napa community for generations. This special 90-minute walking tour explores some of the cemetery’s oldest sections while sharing the stories of historic figures who helped shape Napa Valley. Beginning at the Juarez Building just inside Tulocay’s original gates, the tour is led by a knowledgeable Tulocay Cemetery intern. Complimentary maps and whisper headsets are provided to help guests follow along throughout the experience. The cemetery’s paved paths include steep and hilly areas, so comfortable walking shoes are recommended. Guests using scooters, walkers, or other mobility aids should ensure their equipment is suitable for inclines. Date: Saturday, October 24, 2026 Location: Tulocay Cemetery, 411 Coombsville Rd., Napa Tickets: $30 for NCHS members; $45 for non-members This popular annual event typically sells out, so advance ticket purchase is recommended.

title: The Santa Rosa Original Certified Farmers Market
location: Luther Burbank Center for the Arts
description: The Santa Rosa Original Certified Farmers Market is a year-round Saturday tradition in Sonoma County, bringing together local farmers, ranchers, food artisans, and neighbors from 8:30 a.m. to 1 p.m. This is not just a place to shop, it's a place to connect directly with the people who grow your food. As a Slow Food Sonoma County award recipient, the market prioritizes integrity, seasonality, and true farm-to-community relationships. Expect peak-season produce harvested just hours before market, pasture-raised meats, fresh flowers, artisan breads, handcrafted goods, and thoughtfully prepared foods that reflect the region's agricultural richness. Visitors can stroll the vibrant open-air market, sample local flavors, and experience Sonoma County's food culture in its most authentic form. Families, chefs, and weekend explorers alike gather here to discover what's growing now and to support small farms that keep our local food system strong. Open every Saturday, rain or shine, the Santa Rosa Original Certified Farmers Market is a cornerstone of the community and a must-visit stop for anyone wanting to taste, shop, and experience Sonoma County at its freshest.
source: North Bay Bohemian, Visit Santa Rosa

title: Antarctica: The Frozen Desert | Photographs by Vegar Abelsnes
description:
1st Street Gallery at WTRSHD will present “Antarctica: The Frozen Desert,” a new body of fine art photography by Vegar Abelsnes, opening September 26th, 2026, and on view September through November.  The exhibition marks a deliberate turn in Abelsnes’ photography; after more than two decades of working in a commercial and advertising capacity, he has embarked on a career as a photo and field guide in the polar regions. The exhibit features work generated over 6 voyages to the Antarctic Peninsula. He is returning to Antarctica in January and will add the Falklands and South Georgia to his list of destinations to guide and photograph.

Traveling to some of the most remote and inhospitable coastlines on Earth, Abelsnes has photographed a landscape that exists almost entirely outside of human time. The ice in these images began forming millions of years ago, while Homo sapiens have only existed for roughly 300,000 years. Defined by such a scale, Antarctica is less a place than a record — vast, indifferent, treacherous, and staggeringly beautiful, holding a kind of cosmic truth that Abelsnes says is more important now than ever before.

Parenting in Practice is open to the broader community, including parents of younger children and teenagers. Admission is free and includes access to all sessions. 

Panel Details Below: 

What to Consider When Choosing a School, featuring: Percy L. Abram, Head of School at Sonoma Academy; Tracie Mastronicola, Head of School at The Healdsburg School; Cecily Stock, Head of School at The Presentation School; and Brad Weaver, Head of School at Sonoma Country Day School.

How to Succeed in College \(and Life\), on helping your child to find the intersection between achievement, fulfillment, and joy featuring Dan Lerner, NYU Professor and Author of U Thrive.

Jason Craige Harris, Educator and CEO of Perception Strategies on teaching kids about agency, boundaries, healthy relationships, and the responsible use of power through healthy relationships and communication.

Lori Getz, Internet safety expert and founder of Cyber Education Consultants on keeping kids safe online.

Dr. Devorah Heitner, author of Growing Up in Public: Coming of Age in a Digital World and Screenwise: Helping Kids Thrive \(and Survive\) in Their Digital World on helping your kids manage the effects of social media and digital communication.

title: Park Rx—Intermediate Hiking for Fitness Fall 2026
description:
The program leaders will guide you on 8 weekly hikes with the challenge increasing each week. Leaders will have group discussions about gear, hydration, hiking poles, first aid and pacing, etc. The group's final hike aims for Bald Mountain, where hikers can enjoy stunning vistas.

The following is a list of possible routes specifically selected for this hiking series: 

1) Sat 9/26 — Creekside + Waterfall loop, 3.6 miles, 750 ft elevation \[meet @ White Barn\] 2) Sat 10/03 – Vista Trail loop, 3.4 miles, 830 ft elevation \[meet @ White Barn\] 3) Sat 10/10 – Hillside to Neptune table + Meadow, 4.4 miles, 970 ft elevation \[meet @ White Barn\] 4) Sat 10/17 – Goodspeed to Nattkemper bench, 3.8 miles, 1,240 ft elevation \[meet @ Goodspeed lot\] 5) Sat 10/24 – Hillside + Vista Trail loop, 3.6 miles, 1,070 ft elevation \[meet @ White Barn\] 6) Sat 10/31 – False Lake Meadow & Lake Ilsanjo loop in Trionne-Annadel SP, 6.1 miles, 670 ft elevation \[meet @ Annadel's Cobblestone Trailhead\] 7) Sat 11/07 – Fern Lake + Orchard loop in SDC/Jack London SHP, 5.5 miles, 1,460 ft elevation \[meet @ Walnut & North St inside SDC; park on Grove St\] 8) Sat 11/14 – Bald Mtn summit (w/optional Headwaters detour, 5.8 miles), 5.1 miles, 1,670 ft elevation \[meet @ White Barn\]

Please note these routes are subject to change based on the group and weather, as the group does hike in light rains. Wear appropriate footwear for rocky or slippery trails, and layers. Bring water, and if desired, a snack. The group will be limited to 35 participants. 

The hiking series costs $80 (plus a $10 parking fee per visit. Note that the Sugarloaf Annual Pass is $59 and valid at Sugarloaf and Jack London SHP), or free-of-cost for participants with a September 2026 or newer Park Rx from a Sonoma County Medical Provider.

title: Overeaters Anonymous (OA) Newcomer Meeting
description:
**Is Food a Problem for You? You Are Not Alone.**

Overeaters Anonymous (OA) is a fellowship of people who support each other in recovering from compulsive eating and food behaviors. If you feel you have a problem with food, OA welcomes you—no matter what your background, beliefs, or eating habits. 

We hold an in-person newcomer meeting on first, second and fourth **Saturdays of the month from 9:45 - 10:15 AM at** ​**Unitarian Universalist Congregation of Marin, 240 Channing Way, San Rafael CA 94903**. Contact: Sue M. 415-298-6792​. You may view all North Bay OA in-person and online meetings at https://www.northbayoa.org/meetings.html

In OA, members experience **spiritual, emotional, and physical recovery** by practicing the **Twelve Steps** and living by their spiritual principles—one day at a time.

OA is **not** a diet club or calorie-counting program.

Members have different plans of eating.

OA does **not** endorse any specific food plan. 

If food is causing problems in your life, you don’t have to struggle alone. Recovery is possible, and help is available.

**Visit:** https://www.northbayoa.org/

**Find a meeting:** https://www.northbayoa.org/meetings.html

title: Dia de Muertos at Jack London State Historic Park
description:
In recognition of Día de Muertos, Jack London State Historic Park will present two ofrendas in the House of Happy Walls Museum from Oct. 4 to Nov. 6, 2026.

Dia de Muertos, or Day of the Dead, is a tradition that began in Mexican and other Latino cultures.  An ofrenda, Spanish for ‘offering,’ is an altar created to honor and welcome the memory of those who have died.

The Legacy Ofrenda will honor writer and adventurer Jack London, Charmian London, and other individuals connected to the history of the property. Through photographs, reproductions, traditional elements of an ofrenda, and carefully selected symbolic objects, the installation will reflect Jack and Charmian's partnership, writing and travels, their life at Beauty Ranch, their connection to the land, and the legacies they left behind.

The Community Ofrenda will be a shared, participatory offering. Visitors, locals, volunteers, Board members, and employees can contribute a small photograph, written name, memory, drawing or message honoring someone who has passed away – including a beloved pet. 

The installation will grow throughout October as more people participate.  Materials will be available at the display for visitors who would like to join the celebration and contribute a name, memory or even a drawing of their loved one.

EAMES & EAMES: Meet the couple who Defined Modern Design

Created in collaboration with the Eames Institute of Infinite Curiosity.

EAMES & EAMES explores the iterative, hands-on, and human-centered approach of Charles & Ray Eames. Through furniture, toys, paintings, graphics, and personal belongings collected over their lifetimes, this groundbreaking exhibition looks beyond the iconic Eames chairs to reveal the breadth of their creative practice. More than any single object, their work opened doors to new and unexpected ways of seeing, thinking, making, and understanding the world—ideas that continue to inspire us today.

Curated by Llisa Demetrios, Co-Founder & The Lucia Eames Chief Curator of the Eames Institute of Infinite Curiosity.

title: A Taste of Italy at Centennial Mountain Tasting Room
description:
For wine drinkers eager to experience world-class wines made in California from Italian varieties, the Centennial Mountain Tasting Room is a must during any trip to Sonoma County. Located just off the plaza in the charming town of Healdsburg near famed restaurants, boutiques and galleries, the Centennial Mountain Tasting Room is a destination that invites discovery. Founded by the acclaimed team that guides renowned Pinot Noir and Chardonnay producer Rhys Vineyards, Centennial Mountain was established to explore Italian grape varieties grown on its acclaimed Centennial Mountain Vineyard in the rugged mountains of Northern Sonoma County.

The Centennial Mountain Vineyard Tasting features the winery’s coveted Nebbiolo, and the pioneering Carricante and Nerello Mascalese wines, among others. To showcase how beautifully the wines pair with food, the winery also offers a delicious Wine and Sushi Pairing from nearby Asahi Sushi, one of Healdsburg’s most popular dining destinations.

Guests can also enhance their tasting experience with a curated salumi board from Journeyman Meat Company. This generous accompaniment features six house-made salumi, crostini, cornichons, olives, and a selection of local cheese that serves 2 to 5 guests.

title: Art Exhibit: Aspirations
description:
Date: FOR IMMEDIATE RELEASE  9/15/26

**OCTOBER EXHIBIT: ASPIRATIONS**

EXHIBIT DATES **– September 28 – October 25, 2026**

**RECEPTION: SATURDAY, October 3, 2026, 3-6 pm: Join us to meet Laura Roney and Linda Loveland Reid and learn about their art and inspiration.  Be sure to take part in the Gallery’s free monthlong drawing for a beautiful work by a Gallery artist.  Refreshments will be served.**

Sonoma County artist, **Laura Roney,** unveils **Aspirations**, a new collection of paintings in oil, celebrating the unique differing goals people set during our lives, challenging us to take bold steps forward.  Of universal inspiration**, Aspiration and Awe** splashes the Milky Way’s starry brilliance across the heavens, capturing our imagination and hope as worldly cares are left behind.  Moving from natural forces to human endeavor, looking toward social change, **Aspiring to Vote**, the portrait of a hopeful suffragette, evokes the dream for a better future.  A lifetime goal for many, the marathon, **Aspiring for 26.2,** captures the early morning excitement waiting for start times.  “People doing ordinary things but dreaming larger for the future has been a great inspiration for this series.  I hope folks will be inspired by the boldness of people’s dreams,” commented Roney on her inspiration for the work.

Art has been a lifelong passion for Roney.  Beginning her art studies at a young age, whatever avenue she was pursuing in life, she continued her artistic endeavors.  After a successful career in microbiology and pharmaceutical research, a family move to Northern California enabled Roney to focus on her art.  She received her MFA from Academy of Art University, San Francisco.

Meet the artist: Roney will host the Gallery on September 30 and October 1 from 11am to 6 pm.

The Stairway Smallworks Showcase features Linda Loveland Reid’s **Intentional Chaos,** a collection of exciting mixed-media works that explode with excitement and energy. Random patterns, amorphous shapes and dancing dribbles magically coalesce into bold statements.  Intriguing and compelling, like interlocking gears, in **Patterns of Memory** multiple patterns interlock on fields of gold and black.  “I love throwing ink, paint and even coffee onto a blank canvas and creating through instinct, gesture and emotion.  Distilling energy into smaller works brings new challenges and some happy surprises,” noted Reid on her creative process.

Meet the artist: Reid will host the Gallery on October 23 from 11am to 6 pm.

 Also join us for **ART NITE HEALDSBURG**, Thursday, October 1, 5 – 7 pm.  ART NITE Healdsburg, held the 1st Thursday of Every Month, is a community event celebrating art and creativity with over 20 galleries participating.  ArtNiteHealdsburg.com.

Upstairs Art Gallery, 306 Center Street, Healdsburg, CA 95448. (707) 431-4214.: OPEN DAILY: 11am – 6 pm.    **www.upstairsart gallery.net** 

For further information: Contact: Beverly Bird, Press Contact, at bvdrio@sonic.net or 707-799-1490.

title: Salsa Beginners 2 - Saturdays
description:
Ready to take your salsa to the next level? You’ve mastered the basics, now it’s time to add some flair and fluidity to your salsa dancing.

Pre-requisite: Salsa Beginners 1 – You know your basic steps, left turn, right turn, cross-body lead, and you hold your frame.

**What You’ll Learn**

We’ve curated a curriculum designed to build your confidence and your “social dance” vocabulary:

**• The Cross Body Lead (CBL) Series:** Master both **Inside and Outside Turns**, the essential building blocks for moving your partner across the floor with grace.

**• The “I Turn – You Turn”:** A classic social dance staple that develops timing and hand-change coordination.

**• The Walk-Through:** Learn how to transition smoothly through the dance space without breaking your rhythm.

**• Footwork & Shine:** We’ll break down the footwork pattern that adds personality to your “shines.”

**Technique & Artistry**

Dancing is about more than just where your feet go. In this level, we dive deeper into the “how”:

**• The Frame:** Understand the “tension and compression” needed to lead and follow clearly without using muscle.

**• Upper Body Mechanics:** Learn how to isolate your ribcage and shoulders to move with that authentic Latin soul.

**• Connection:** Developing a “heavy” but responsive arm connection to ensure your partner feels every lead.

**Important Details**

**• No dance experience required:** Whether you’ve never danced before or it’s been a while, you’re welcome here!

**• No partner necessary:** Come solo or bring a friend—either way, you’ll have plenty of opportunities to dance.

**•** Please wear **non-marking shoe soles:** This helps us keep our dance floor in great condition.

Date & Time:

**Thursdays 7:30 PM**

**Saturday 11:00 AM**

Instructor: Lucie Ebnerova

Address: 4140 Redwood Highway #8 San Rafael, CA

Note: Arrive 10 minutes before. No floor marking shoe soles allowed.

description:
Join us for an unforgettable afternoon where fashion, wine, and philanthropy come together in the heart of Napa Valley.

Hosted at Frank Family Vineyards, this exclusive event celebrates our collaboration with Simkhai in support of Dress for Success, an organization dedicated to empowering women to achieve economic independence through career development, professional attire, and a global network of support.

The experience begins with a wine reception followed by a beautifully curated multi-course lunch by Bottega Napa Valley. As guests are seated on our Miller House Lawn, enjoy an inspiring panel conversation featuring Frank Family Founder, Leslie Frank, acclaimed fashion designer Jonathan Simkhai, and Dress for Success CEO Joanie Bily. Together, they'll discuss the power of purpose-driven partnerships, confidence, and self-expression through fashion and wine.

Guests will then enjoy an exclusive runway presentation of the Simkhai pieces, culminating in the debut of our limited-edition collaborative wine, created to celebrate craftsmanship, creativity, and giving back.

Throughout the afternoon, renowned color analyst, The Color Countess, will offer personalized color analysis sessions, helping guests discover the colors that best complement their natural features while celebrating confidence through personal style.

Every ticket purchased, along with a percentage of proceeds from featured wine and Simkhai apparel sales during the event, will directly support Dress for Success and its purpose to help women thrive in work and in life.

We invite you to experience an afternoon of exceptional wine, inspiring conversation, timeless fashion, and meaningful impact.

title: What We Can Know by Ian McEwan [OPTION 1]
description:
Novel Lovers of Sonoma County, CA
***What We Can Know* by Ian McEwan**

**Ed's description**: "It is 2119, and Thomas Metcalfe is a humanities academic expert on the 90 30 era - 1990 to 2030 - when the Derangement accelerated leading eventually to the Inundation which destroyed much of the civilized world with ephemeral archives preserved in mountainous libraries while Nigeria houses ALL digital records. Thomas embarks on a hero's journey to find the long lost but legendary 'Corona for Vivien' recited by the famed poet Francis Blundy for his wife's fiftieth birthday party at an 'immortal night' with literary luminaries in 2014. In this period the STEM colleges have all the best students and facilities while Humanities colleges have the lousiest students and facilities, and Thomas hopes his finding of the corona - a poetic structure usually of seven sonnets but 15 in this case - will spark some life in his dying field. He finds Vivien's memoirs, and the second part of the novel belongs to her."

**Lucinda**: "This book was a mind bender. I never quite knew what was going on until the very end. I believe that’s the whole point. I appreciated McEwan’s views on climate decline and what it might lead to. It was thought provoking (no spoilers). I also found the book a little hard to read as it was quite detailed, and the characters might be considered amoral. There is a lot here."

**Dave**: "Intriguing novel. Pondering the future not about technological change but what will do with the vast amount of saved data. How will we encounter our history and the place for humanities in the future."

**Nancy R**: "I've started on my second reading. There's so much in the book to discuss. One thing is 100 years in the future calling global warming 'the derangement.' brilliant, among others. The story is involving and well written, and is sure to generate lively discussions."

*•* "Sophisticated entertainment of a high order." —*The New York Times*
*• "*Brilliantly, and surprisingly, plotted."—*The Washington Post •* "A novelist of consummate skill."—*The Wall Street Journal*
*•* "Elegantly structured and provocative."—*Los Angeles Times*

Celebrate America’s musical heritage with Sing Napa Valley at the *American Songbook Singer Showcase*. Presented in honor of the United States’ 250th anniversary, this lively afternoon concert travels from the 1920s through the early 1960s with jazz standards, Broadway favorites, and memorable songs from film. Two concerts: Saturday, October 24 & Sunday, October 25 at 3pm.

Whether these classics are lifelong favorites or brand-new discoveries, *American Songbook Singer Showcase* promises an uplifting celebration of music’s power to bridge generations and bring people together.

Enjoy timeless music by George and Ira Gershwin, Cole Porter, Hoagy Carmichael, and Irving Berlin, including favorites such as “Mr. Sandman,” “Honeysuckle Rose,” “Night and Day,” and “Dream a Little Dream of Me.” Sing Napa Valley choir members and special guests will take the spotlight in solos, duets, trios, and small ensembles, joined by collaborative pianist Anthony Mayor. title: Documentary:  JAMES McNEIL WHISTLER
description:
Whistler was a loud and fascinating character who lived life to the full. But above all, and despite all the legal scandals and verbal posturing, he was a magnificent painter, printmaker and writer. An extremely proficient and imaginative artist with a gift for creativity and expression that embraced the cult of beauty, pushed the boundaries of painting and gave birth to modern art. 

Tate Britain is now holding the first major retrospective of Whistler in three decades. This blockbuster exhibition promises to reawaken the world to just how important Whistler is to art history, uniting world-famous masterpieces with rarely seen works. Exhibition on Screen will bring these stunning works and the incredible story behind them to cinemas around the world while the exhibition is still running, bringing this truly global artist to a global audience. This will be an unmissable chance to get to know this visually spectacular artist and the influence he has had on those who followed.

title: Fresh Cheesemaking with Botanical Flavors
description:
Fresh cheese is one of the most approachable and rewarding things to make at home. In Sonoma County’s rich dairy landscape, these simple cheeses have long been a staple—equally at home in everyday meals and on a shared table.

In this hands-on workshop, you’ll learn how to make fresh cheeses from cow and goat milk, while exploring how herbs, flowers, and citrus can shape flavor in simple, elegant ways. We’ll cover the essential techniques behind fresh cheesemaking so you can confidently recreate them in your own kitchen.

In this workshop you’ll:

• Learn the fundamentals of fresh cheesemaking using cow and goat milk

• Understand key concepts in cheesemaking, including acidity, texture, and food safety

• Make goat milk chèvre with edible flowers and with rosemary and honey

• Prepare fresh ricotta with Meyer lemon

• Explore how to incorporate herbs, flowers, and other botanicals into your cheeses

You’ll work alongside instructor Willow, a Sonoma County farmer and educator, whose approach connects practical kitchen skills with a deeper understanding of ingredients and process.

You’ll leave with recipes, techniques, and the confidence to begin making fresh cheese at home.

No prior cheesemaking experience required.

description:
This fall, Buena Vista Winery invites you to uncover the mysteries, legends, and ghostly encounters woven into more than 165 years of history. Led by Sonoma historian and actor George Webber, this immersive 90 minute experience journeys through the historic Press House and Champagne Cellars, revealing true tales of unexplained happenings reported by Buena Vista team members and visitors throughout the years.

Hear the stories of the Glowing Ghostly Shirt, the Little Girl Who Says Hi, the mysterious Ghost Party on the Second Floor, the Old Man Who Walked Into a Stone Wall, and other strange occurrences that continue to add to the legend of Buena Vista.

Along the way, explore some of the winery’s most intriguing spaces, including the Bubble Lounge, Cave of Curiosities, and Wine Tool Museum, while enjoying five Buena Vista wines tasted throughout the experience, including a taste drawn directly from barrel.

And, as with any journey through Buena Vista’s extraordinary past, you never quite know when the winery’s legendary founder, Count Agoston Haraszthy, may choose to make an appearance.

History, wine, mystery, and perhaps a spirit or two await.

title: Blue Note Napa Summer Sessions
description:
It’s been a full quarter-century since a young saxophonist and composer released his debut recording as a leader, Trust. On September 1, 2017, Boney James released his 16th album, this one titled Honestly. If you sense a direct line between those titles, you’ve already come a long way toward understanding what motivates the four-time GRAMMY nominee and multi-platinum-selling musician.

“I’m fighting the good fight to be my own artist and not be pigeonholed,” says the genre-blurring James. “With a record’s title I always try to find something that will communicate the feeling I get when I listen to it. The feeling I get with this music is a sense of sincerity and intimacy. The word ‘honestly’ really reflects how I aspire to live my life and create my music. These are interesting times we are living in and the one thing I can do with the skills that I have is to make music that evokes a feeling and takes people somewhere… to do what I can to try and make the world a more pleasant place.”

Honestly follows futuresoul, James’ 2015 release which spent eleven weeks at \#1 on the Billboard Contemporary Jazz Chart. The New York Times raved, “Boney James performs with panache...His arc as a soloist is emotional...he can paint a scene.” Honestly, says James, is quite different sounding than the previous record. “It’s more exposed,” he says of the 10-track collection. “A number of the songs have a more buoyant, cheerful, happy quality to them.” James produced the record and co-wrote all but one track, his interpretation of the Johnny Mercer-Hoagy Carmichael classic ‘Skylark.’

His skill as a performer as well as a recording artist garnered this notice from the Boston Globe, “James swaggered across the stage like a blacktop hero draining treys on an over-matched opponent. He even weaved his way through the audience, never missing a beat and all but daring the crowd not to have a good time."

Over the years, James has racked up sales of more than three million records, four RIAA gold albums, four GRAMMY nominations, a Soul Train Award, nominations for two NAACP Image Awards and 10 CDs atop Billboard’s Contemporary Jazz Albums chart. In 2009, Billboard named him one of the Top 3 Contemporary Jazz Artists Of The Decade along with Kenny G and Norah Jones.

With Honestly, as with futuresoul and the GRAMMY-nominated The Beat before it, Boney James is making some of the most stellar, wholly realized music of his career. “I’ve just grown up, personally and musically,” he says. “I’m a lot calmer now when I approach making music and have more confidence. I’m a “give-110 percent” kind of person and I’m enjoying the process more now. I think that comes out in the music. Maybe that’s why this new record is so much fun to listen to. There are parts on the record that still make me smile.”

title: Patrick Ball: Celtic Harp & Story
location: Occidental Center for the Arts, 3850 Doris Murphy Court, Occidental
description:
Step into the enchanting world of
Patrick Ball
, one of the premier Celtic harp players in the world and a captivating storyteller whose performances weave music, legend, wit, and wonder into an unforgettable experience.
With the crystalline beauty of the Celtic harp as his musical voice, Ball brings ancient Irish tales and timeless melodies vividly to life, transporting audiences to a world of heroes and dreamers, mystery and mischief, heartbreak and humor. His masterful playing and gift for storytelling create an evening that is at once intimate, magical, and deeply human.
Join us at Occidental Center for the Arts for a spellbinding journey through the music and stories of Ireland with a true master of the tradition.
Tickets are $35, $30 for OCA members. Doors open at 6:30 PM, refreshments available. Art gallery open during event.
Get Tickets
About Patrick Ball:
Whether in the stronghold of a Galway chieftain in the years before history began or yesterday in the snug corner of a pub in Dublin, the Irish have always delighted in storytelling. Their passion for eloquence and wordplay, their deep devotion to their mythical past, their ability to find joy and humor in a dark world, and their belief that the supernatural world could appear between one breath and the next made their stories and the telling of them unrivaled in the world of the oral tradition.
And always, amidst the storytelling, there was music. Jigs, reels and haunting airs graced the spaces between the tales. And first among Irish instruments, and the most honored, was the legendary Celtic harp. With its crystalline, bell-like voice and lavish resonance, it would soothe its listeners and lead them deeper into the realms of the imagination.
In
Celtic Harp and Story
Patrick Ball rekindles the fire and wonder of an evening of Irish storytelling. For in telling the marvelous old tales of wit and enchantment, and in playing the ancient, brass-strung harp of Ireland, he not only carries on two of the richest traditions of Celtic culture, but blends them in concert to create “a warm and magical performance.”
“An American master of the Irish instrument, a peripatetic modern day bard, combining tale-telling, history and music into a seamless compound that reaches all ages and types of listeners.”—San Francisco Chronicle
“It’s rare that we will feature a performer on our fine performances season for two consecutive years, but then Patrick is a rare artist ... The audience was entranced by his harp playing, amused by his storytelling. Patrick is a grand man who puts on a great show.”—APAP Report / Humboldt State University
“The SRO audience loved Mr. Ball's performance, asking when we will be bringing him back. Ball was a delight to work with, very professional, and he is superb at captivating an audience.”—APAP Report / Arizona State University
“Patrick Ball conjured some Druid magic ... weaving words and music into a spellbinding program.”—The Blade, Toledo, OH
source: Occidental Center for the Arts, North Bay Bohemian

title: Rocky Horror Picture Show With Full Shadow Cast and Costume Contest
description:
**Don’t dream it. Be it!**

Sonoma Valley Pride is bringing **The Rocky Horror Picture Show** back to the historic Sebastiani Theatre for our **second annual screening and costume contest** — and this year, we’re taking it to a whole new level.

For the first time, Rocky comes to life with a **full shadow cast performed by San Francisco’s Bawdy Caste**!

Watch the cult classic on the big screen while a live cast performs along with the film right in front of you. Expect outrageous audience participation, **props for throwing**, ridiculous costumes, plenty of callbacks, and a costume contest celebrating your very best Rocky Horror looks.

Whether you’ve been doing the Time Warp for decades or this is your first trip to Frankenstein Place, come ready for a night of camp, chaos, community, and absolute fun.

**All proceeds benefit Sonoma Valley Pride!** 

**Schedule**

**6:30 PM — Doors Open**

Come early, grab your seat, show off your look, and get ready for the night.

**7:00 PM — Pre-Show & Costume Contest**

We’ll kick things off with our costume contest, pre-show festivities, and all the preparation you need before the madness begins.

**7:40 PM — The Rocky Horror Picture Show + Live Shadow Cast**

The film begins with **SF’s Bawdy Caste performing live alongside the movie.**

**Guests are highly encouraged to come dressed as their favorite Rocky Horror character** — or simply embrace the spirit of the night and wear something fabulous, outrageous, strange, glamorous, or completely over the top.

Prizes will be awarded to some of our favorite looks of the evening.

And yes — **audience participation is strongly encouraged.**

**Remembering a Legend**

This year’s screening will be especially bittersweet following the passing of **Tim Curry**, whose unforgettable portrayal of Dr. Frank-N-Furter helped make *The Rocky Horror Picture Show* the cultural phenomenon it is today.

For generations, Rocky Horror has permitted people to be louder, stranger, freer, more theatrical, and more unapologetically themselves.

This October, we’ll gather together to celebrate Tim Curry, the character he made iconic, and the enduring spirit of individuality, freedom, and queer joy that continues to make Rocky Horror so meaningful.

So grab your fishnets, warm up your Time Warp, gather your friends, and join Sonoma Valley Pride for one unforgettable night at the Sebastiani Theatre.

**SF's Bawdy Caste**

The Bawdy Caste is San Francisco’s legendary Rocky Horror shadow cast, bringing glitter, fishnets, irreverence, and unapologetic camp to stages across the Bay Area and beyond for three decades.

More than a performance troupe, The Bawdy Caste celebrates individuality, acceptance, and community. Their stage is a space where people can be loud, strange, expressive, and fully themselves — creating an inclusive environment where everyone is encouraged to feel seen, welcomed, and part of the fun.

title: Phil Johnson and Roadside Attraction Comedy and Music
description:
Headlining!

Phil Johnson delivers a high-energy comedy experience that blends stand-up and live music. With a sharp eye for the absurd, he tackles topics like American exceptionalism, body image, conspiracy culture, and the general weirdness of modern life — all from the viewpoint of a guy who happily grew up in the deeply multi-everything community of the San Francisco Bay Area.

His material is smart, satirical, and unafraid to ask bigger questions while still chasing the laugh.

Phil has performed at the Sundance Film Festival and Edinburgh Fringe Festival, his stand-up tracks air on SiriusXM Radio, and he's been heard on Bob & Tom Radio and seen on Amazon Prime. He has released four comedy specials and multiple albums and singles, showcasing a signature blend of tightly written jokes, catchy \(and occasionally naughty\) songs, and a performer's instinct for balancing insight with irreverence.

title: Sweeney Todd
description:
Sweeney Todd is largely considered one of Stephen Sondheim’s masterpieces. With it, he aimed to create a musical that could “scare the hell out of everyone,” and yet, somehow, be funny.

The story centers around Sweeney Todd, an unjustly exiled barber who returns to London, seeking vengeance against the lecherous judge who framed him and ravaged his young wife. The road to revenge leads Todd to Mrs. Lovett, a resourceful proprietress of a failing pie shop, above which, he opens a new barber practice. Mrs. Lovett’s luck sharply shifts when Todd’s thirst for blood inspires the integration of an ingredient into her meat pies that has the people of 19th Century London lining up…and the carnage has only just begun!

\***Content Advisory:** Adult language and violent themes, as well as controversial pie recipes. Recommended for 12+.

Running Time: 2 hours, 40 minutes including one intermission.

title: Big Brother & The Holding Company
description: The band was formed by Peter Albin, Sam Andrew, James Gurley and Chuck Jones in San Francisco, in a Victorian mansion/boarding house owned by Peter's uncle at 1090 Page Street in the Haight-Ashbury. That house became the site of Wednesday night jam sessions which were organized by Chet Helms who was the real "Big Brother," naming the band, bringing James Gurley into the fold and later seeing that his old friend Janis Joplin came to sing with them. The first official Big Brother gig was at the Open Theater in Berkeley, January 1966. Within a short time they became the house band for Chet at the Avalon Ballroom and began to develop a loyal following, largely due to the charismatic, pioneering guitarwork of James Gurley. The band had what Sam Andrew callled a "progressive-regressive hurricane blues style," playing such tunes as Hall of the Mountain King, Coo Coo, That's How Strong My Love Is, and Down On Me. Janis Joplin made her debut with Big Brother at the Avalon Ballroom in June 1966, and a year later, in June 1967, Big Brother and Janis performed at The Monterey Pop Festival. From that point on, Janis became the main focus of attention, with her high voltage and raw emotional performances, while Big Brother faded into the backgroud and became known for being her back-up band.

title: Safari West Presents! Amigos Alados
description: Conservation Dinner Series: Alison Quoyeser of  Amigos Alados joins us in the elephant room after dinner to give a talk about migratory songbirds in North America. The conservation dinner series is complimentary to all dinner guests. If you want to attend this presentation, please call our reservations team at \(707\) 566-3667 or \(800\) 616-2695 and they can book it for you. Dinner starts at 7:00 PM.    About the Speaker: Alison is the Co-Founder \(with Martina Gögelmann\) and Co-Director of Amigos Alados. She works with students along the Pacific Flyway to raise awareness of birds and their habitats, watershed ecology, and environmental restoration, as well as to instill cultural appreciation of our friends in Mexico who share the same migratory birds. After working as an architect for 10 years, Alison taught second and fourth grade for 28 years, and with her students designed and planted a campus habitat garden to attract birds and beneficial insects. Creating hands-on curriculum, project-based learning opportunities, and musical/theatrical performances to teach about the environment, she focused on the rainforest ecosystem as a second grade teacher and then local watershed ecology and ornithology as a fourth grade teacher. Sinceretiring from full-time teaching in2017, Alison has expanded her work with Amigos Alados and has served as a faculty member of STRAW \(Students and Teachers Restoring a Watershed\), which is the educational arm of Point Blue Conservation Science. A good number of Amigos Alados teachers are also members of STRAW. Alison has studied the Spanish language for many years as a child and as an adult and is pleased that she gets to use her Spanish almost daily in communication with the Amigos Alados co-director in Mexico.

In OA, members experience spiritual, emotional, and physical recovery by practicing the Twelve Steps and living by their spiritual principles—one day at a time.

Overeaters Anonymous \(OA\) is a fellowship of people who support each other in recovering from compulsive eating and food behaviors. If you feel you have a problem with food, OA welcomes you—no matter what your background, beliefs, or eating habits. 

We hold an in-person meetings at 9:30 on Sunday mornings at Church of the Nazarene, 18980 Arnold Drive, Sonoma, CA \(a small room directly off of parking lot; look for the sign posted\) and newcomers are always welcome.

You may view all North Bay OA in-person and online meetings at https://www.northbayoa.org/meetings.html

OA is not a diet club or calorie-counting program.

Members have different plans of eating.

OA does not endorse any specific food plan. 

Visit: https://www.northbayoa.org/

EAMES & EAMES: Meet the couple who Defined Modern Design

Created in collaboration with the Eames Institute of Infinite Curiosity.

EAMES & EAMES explores the iterative, hands-on, and human-centered approach of Charles & Ray Eames. Through furniture, toys, paintings, graphics, and personal belongings collected over their lifetimes, this groundbreaking exhibition looks beyond the iconic Eames chairs to reveal the breadth of their creative practice. More than any single object, their work opened doors to new and unexpected ways of seeing, thinking, making, and understanding the world—ideas that continue to inspire us today.

Curated by Llisa Demetrios, Co-Founder & The Lucia Eames Chief Curator of the Eames Institute of Infinite Curiosity.

title: The Art of Paste Paper
location: North Bay Letterpress Arts, 925d Gravenstein Hwy South, Sebastopol, CA, 95472, United States
description:
Paste paper is one of the oldest decorated papers used by bookbinders, and can be found in books that are centuries old. Hundreds of years ago (a tradition that continues today), bookbinders would sometimes use up their leftover bookbinding paste by adding pigment to the mixture and brushing it out on surfaces to make decorative papers used in bookbinding. They would make strokes or stipple patterns with a brush in the paste, or use tools to draw or comb designs in the paper and then let it dry. 
One of the distinctive qualities of paste paper is the rich 3-dimensional patterns and designs. This is achieved because when the paste is first applied to the paper and a pattern is made, the paste is thick with peaks and valleys. As the paper dries, the paste is sucked flat into the paper, leaving a 3-dimensional pattern on a 2-dimensional surface. 
During this workshop students will learn about the history of paste paper. Together we will look at different samples and use different kinds of paste and tools to create decorative paper. This fun class focuses on color blending, textures, and graphic design on paper for artistic use in a variety of book arts or collage-focused art projects. Anything but ordinary, this is a hands-on class where participants will create beautiful custom decorative papers by applying colored starch paste to paper and manipulating it with tools to create patterns. Students will learn different recipes for making paste, how to create tools for mark making, and each individual will take home a full suite of papers made in this single session. 
This special workshop welcomes beginners, and artists of all levels. The instructor will offer guided instruction in a supportive learning environment with a limited class size. The class materials fee will include paper and all the tools needed to create each of these projects. 
Please note that since the papers need to dry before they can be safely taken home, students should arrange a time for later pick-up from our studio.

title: Art Exhibit: Aspirations
description:
Date: FOR IMMEDIATE RELEASE  9/15/26

**OCTOBER EXHIBIT: ASPIRATIONS**

EXHIBIT DATES **– September 28 – October 25, 2026**

**RECEPTION: SATURDAY, October 3, 2026, 3-6 pm: Join us to meet Laura Roney and Linda Loveland Reid and learn about their art and inspiration.  Be sure to take part in the Gallery’s free monthlong drawing for a beautiful work by a Gallery artist.  Refreshments will be served.**

Sonoma County artist, **Laura Roney,** unveils **Aspirations**, a new collection of paintings in oil, celebrating the unique differing goals people set during our lives, challenging us to take bold steps forward.  Of universal inspiration**, Aspiration and Awe** splashes the Milky Way’s starry brilliance across the heavens, capturing our imagination and hope as worldly cares are left behind.  Moving from natural forces to human endeavor, looking toward social change, **Aspiring to Vote**, the portrait of a hopeful suffragette, evokes the dream for a better future.  A lifetime goal for many, the marathon, **Aspiring for 26.2,** captures the early morning excitement waiting for start times.  “People doing ordinary things but dreaming larger for the future has been a great inspiration for this series.  I hope folks will be inspired by the boldness of people’s dreams,” commented Roney on her inspiration for the work.

Art has been a lifelong passion for Roney.  Beginning her art studies at a young age, whatever avenue she was pursuing in life, she continued her artistic endeavors.  After a successful career in microbiology and pharmaceutical research, a family move to Northern California enabled Roney to focus on her art.  She received her MFA from Academy of Art University, San Francisco.

Meet the artist: Roney will host the Gallery on September 30 and October 1 from 11am to 6 pm.

The Stairway Smallworks Showcase features Linda Loveland Reid’s **Intentional Chaos,** a collection of exciting mixed-media works that explode with excitement and energy. Random patterns, amorphous shapes and dancing dribbles magically coalesce into bold statements.  Intriguing and compelling, like interlocking gears, in **Patterns of Memory** multiple patterns interlock on fields of gold and black.  “I love throwing ink, paint and even coffee onto a blank canvas and creating through instinct, gesture and emotion.  Distilling energy into smaller works brings new challenges and some happy surprises,” noted Reid on her creative process.

Meet the artist: Reid will host the Gallery on October 23 from 11am to 6 pm.

 Also join us for **ART NITE HEALDSBURG**, Thursday, October 1, 5 – 7 pm.  ART NITE Healdsburg, held the 1st Thursday of Every Month, is a community event celebrating art and creativity with over 20 galleries participating.  ArtNiteHealdsburg.com.

title: Coffee & Collage
description:
Coffee and Collage is Autonomous Gallery’s monthly gathering for making art, sharing space, and connecting with community.

In collaboration with TBD Coffee, we invite you to slow down, grab a cup of coffee, and spend some time making something with your hands. We provide the collage materials, tools, and inspiration. You bring your curiosity.

There’s no experience required and no expectation to make anything “good.” Cut, tear, layer, rearrange, obscure, discover. Make a mess. Follow an idea wherever it takes you. Or just sit at the table and see what happens.

At Autonomous, we believe creative spaces should be accessible, welcoming, and built around collective care rather than competition. Coffee and Collage is a chance to practice that together: artists and non-artists, longtime friends and people meeting for the first time, all sharing a table and making something side by side.

All materials provided. All skill levels welcome.

Suggested donation: $25.

Come Caffeinate and create with us!

title: S.R. Laws
description:
S.R. Laws: An inspiring Storyteller in Song

        S.R. Laws is a performing and recording original musical artist whose work resonates with a familiar warmth while introducing entirely fresh ideas. Hailed by guitarist/promoter Scotty O’Neill as “an ORIGINAL songwriter who knows how to tell a story clearly in song,” Laws has built a reputation for songs that capture both nostalgia and innovation.

Early Influences and Musical Roots  

Growing up in Northern California, Laws developed a deep bond with music at an early age. His father worked as a trash collector, and young Scott Ray Laws \(a.k.a. S.R. Laws\) spent countless hours digging through discarded 45-rpm records. Each discovery—whether caked in grime or found pristine—felt like unearthing treasure. The thrill of dropping the needle on something new ignited his lifelong passion for song-craft.

The Texas Pilgrimage  

With only two suitcases and $500 to his name, Laws set out for Austin, Texas—the “Live Music Capital of the World.” There, open‐mic nights and songwriter showcases became his classroom. Night after night, he honed his craft, forging connections and absorbing the essence of Americana, roots rock, and modern folk.

 “It was such a treat catching your set last night—really refreshing to hear something new and original. Thanks for pulling up a chair and hanging out with us—we really enjoyed the conversation and the stories behind your songs.” - Tripp B., Singer-Songwriter

Influences That Shaped His Voice  

Laws draws inspiration from master storytellers who paved the way for heartfelt, lyrical music. Artists who have left an indelible mark on his craft include:

- John Hiatt  

- Lucinda Williams  

- Rodney Crowell  

- Neil Finn  

- Patty Griffin  

- Steve Earle  

- Ron Sexsmith  

Their mastery of narrative and melody has shaped his own artistic journey, resulting in songs that feel both comfortingly familiar and entirely “out there.”

Critical Acclaim  

Colleagues and venue owners alike have praised his work and stage presence:  

“Scott Ray Laws is a unique and really cool songwriter…he digs into materials, tells a story in his songs, and has a clean baritone vocality that is easy on the ears. We had a chance to meet and hang with Scott back in May…and I had to have him back for a Wednesday evening.” - Luigi, Owner of The Listening Room

“Expect slow-burning passion and vivid music…the kind of energy that turns into ‘let’s stay for just one more!” - Doug, Owner/Wine Maker at Spicy Vines

Current Projects  

Now based in Sonoma County, California, Laws works tirelessly as a recording, writing & touring artist. Through over 100 gig dates a year, intimate club shows, festival stages, house concerts and late-night songwriter circles, he invites audiences to join him on a musical journey—one heartfelt story at a time.

With a blend of classic influence, modern vision, and a voice that feels like home, S.R. Laws continues to carve out his place in the American songwriting landscape.

Zach Neil is the 2022 Texas Country Music Association’s Male Artist of the Year and has earned five consecutive Top 40 Texas country singles – not bad for a guy who planned to follow in his dad’s footsteps and become a farmer. description: Misalliance is one of George Bernard Shaw’s most spirited and surprising comedies. title: Sweeney Todd
description:
Sweeney Todd is largely considered one of Stephen Sondheim’s masterpieces. With it, he aimed to create a musical that could “scare the hell out of everyone,” and yet, somehow, be funny.

The story centers around Sweeney Todd, an unjustly exiled barber who returns to London, seeking vengeance against the lecherous judge who framed him and ravaged his young wife. The road to revenge leads Todd to Mrs. Lovett, a resourceful proprietress of a failing pie shop, above which, he opens a new barber practice. Mrs. Lovett’s luck sharply shifts when Todd’s thirst for blood inspires the integration of an ingredient into her meat pies that has the people of 19th Century London lining up…and the carnage has only just begun!

\***Content Advisory:** Adult language and violent themes, as well as controversial pie recipes. Recommended for 12+.

title: Sing Napa Valley presents “American Songbook Singer Showcase”
description:
Celebrate America’s musical heritage with Sing Napa Valley at the *American Songbook Singer Showcase*. Presented in honor of the United States’ 250th anniversary, this lively afternoon concert travels from the 1920s through the early 1960s with jazz standards, Broadway favorites, and memorable songs from film. Two concerts: Saturday, October 24 & Sunday, October 25 at 3pm.

Whether these classics are lifelong favorites or brand-new discoveries, *American Songbook Singer Showcase* promises an uplifting celebration of music’s power to bridge generations and bring people together.

Enjoy timeless music by George and Ira Gershwin, Cole Porter, Hoagy Carmichael, and Irving Berlin, including favorites such as “Mr. Sandman,” “Honeysuckle Rose,” “Night and Day,” and “Dream a Little Dream of Me.” Sing Napa Valley choir members and special guests will take the spotlight in solos, duets, trios, and small ensembles, joined by collaborative pianist Anthony Mayor. Bring family and friends for an uplifting celebration of music that connects generations.

title: Haunted Wine Tour & Tasting
description:
This fall, Buena Vista Winery invites you to uncover the mysteries, legends, and ghostly encounters woven into more than 165 years of history. Led by Sonoma historian and actor George Webber, this immersive 90 minute experience journeys through the historic Press House and Champagne Cellars, revealing true tales of unexplained happenings reported by Buena Vista team members and visitors throughout the years.

Hear the stories of the Glowing Ghostly Shirt, the Little Girl Who Says Hi, the mysterious Ghost Party on the Second Floor, the Old Man Who Walked Into a Stone Wall, and other strange occurrences that continue to add to the legend of Buena Vista.

Along the way, explore some of the winery’s most intriguing spaces, including the Bubble Lounge, Cave of Curiosities, and Wine Tool Museum, while enjoying five Buena Vista wines tasted throughout the experience, including a taste drawn directly from barrel.

And, as with any journey through Buena Vista’s extraordinary past, you never quite know when the winery’s legendary founder, Count Agoston Haraszthy, may choose to make an appearance.

History, wine, mystery, and perhaps a spirit or two await.

title: Overeaters Anonymous (OA) Newcomer Meeting in Santa Rosa
description:
**Is Food a Problem for You? You Are Not Alone.**

Overeaters Anonymous (OA) is a fellowship of people who support each other in recovering from compulsive eating and food behaviors. If you feel you have a problem with food, OA welcomes you—no matter what your background, beliefs, or eating habits.

We hold an in-person newcomer meeting on **Sundays from 4:00 – 5:00 PM** **at Christ Church United Methodist, 1717 Yulupa Ave., Room #4, Santa Rosa**. Contact: Abigail (707) 293-5888. You may view all North Bay OA in-person and online meetings at https://www.northbayoa.org/meetings.html .

In OA, members experience **spiritual, emotional, and physical recovery** by practicing the **Twelve Steps** and living by their spiritual principles—one day at a time.

OA is **not** a diet club or calorie-counting program.

Members have different plans of eating.

OA does **not** endorse any specific food plan.

If food is causing problems in your life, you don’t have to struggle alone. Recovery is possible, and help is available.

**Visit:** https://www.northbayoa.org/

**Find a meeting:** https://www.northbayoa.org/meetings.html

title: Poet Jeremy Raikes’s book signing
description:
Poet Jeremy Raikes (well known to many in Sonoma County as the Chair Repair Guy!) will celebrate his 90th birthday and the publication of his poetry collection, *Delicious Suspicions*, with a book signing and birthday gathering on Sunday, October 25, 2026, at 4:00 p.m. at Wonderland Pizzeria, 20391 Highway 116 in Monte Rio.

Raised on a cattle ranch in Argentina by expat British parents, in the 1960's Jeremy was an advertising writer at J Walter Thompson (then the largest advertising agency in the world) and later became creative director of their Mexico City office. While at Thompson, Jeremy collaborated with Charles Schultz on a series of animated Peanuts ads for the Ford Motor Company.

The occasion offers readers a chance to meet Jeremy, purchase a signed copy of his book and celebrate a writer whose work approaches life with humor, tenderness and an enduring sense of wonder.

*Delicious Suspicions* explores love, friendship, loss, aging and the pleasures of everyday encounters. Playful wordplay and conversational rhythms sit alongside candid reflections on sorrow, spiritual faith and human connection. These are poems that acknowledge life’s difficulties while returning, again and again, to affection, gratitude and delight.

One poem’s title, “I’M NOT AS OLD AS I USED TO BE,” offers a fitting introduction to a poet celebrating his 90th birthday with a new book. Elsewhere, a trip to the laundromat becomes an unexpected encounter with love, and a walk along the beach becomes a celebration of companionship.

The gathering combines a literary occasion with a personal milestone: an opportunity to discover Raikes’s poetry and wish its author a happy 90th birthday.

Please note this event is for ages 9 and up. An educational hands-on workshop ·  Learn a new food skill ·  Explore the normally-underwater inter tidal zone at a negative low tide ·  Connect with your local food system ·  Enjoy nutritional-rich umami direct from the source.

title: Petaluma River Full Moon Paddle
description:
Come play on the river at night.

Join The Floathouse for a magical evening paddle on the Petaluma River—Petaluma’s Longest Park—timed to catch the full moon rising over the wetlands just south of downtown. As twilight fades, we’ll head out together in Hobie pedal kayaks for a relaxed, guided glide that turns nighttime into playtime.

These pedal-powered kayaks make the journey smooth and easy, even if there’s a breeze or moving tide. We’ll cruise about a mile and a half downriver to the perfect moonrise vantage point, where calm water, wide skies, and glowing reflections set the scene.

This is a social, feel-good outdoor experience designed for anyone looking for something a little different to do after dark—part nature, part adventure, part pure vibe.

$60 per person includes everything: • Hobie pedal kayak • PFD and safety lights • Experienced local guide • A memorable, moonlit river experience

✨ Easy. Playful. Peaceful. Spend your evening under the full moon—on the water.

title: Marc Cary Trio
description: In a jazz world brimming with brilliant and adventurous pianists, Marc Cary stands apart by way of pedigree and design as one of New York's best jazz pianists. With his Focus Trio, Cary strikes an organic balance between jazz harmonies and rhythms from Africa and India. Drummer and tabla player Sameer Gupta plays an essential role in these rhythms along with bassist David Ewell, who are the original members of the Focus Trio and collaborators for over 20 years. Grammy-nominated pianist Cary brings into sharp focus his many influences-from deep indigenous world rhythms to hard bop to classical lyricism. The energy and the cultural wealth of Harlem, New York resonate in their music. Cary is alternately percussive and subtle, animated and introspective, balancing energy and lyricism with a depth of personal expression that which he calls "classical indigenous jazz for the people." Cary's mission statement for Focus is "to bring indigenous rhythms together with American jazz to create new palettes of sound."

description:

Special breakout sessions are devoted to the interpretation of Doppler hemodynamics, stress echocardiography, multimodality imaging, and congenital heart disease.

title: Antarctica: The Frozen Desert | Photographs by Vegar Abelsnes
description:
1st Street Gallery at WTRSHD will present “Antarctica: The Frozen Desert,” a new body of fine art photography by Vegar Abelsnes, opening September 26th, 2026, and on view September through November.  The exhibition marks a deliberate turn in Abelsnes’ photography; after more than two decades of working in a commercial and advertising capacity, he has embarked on a career as a photo and field guide in the polar regions. The exhibit features work generated over 6 voyages to the Antarctic Peninsula. He is returning to Antarctica in January and will add the Falklands and South Georgia to his list of destinations to guide and photograph.

Traveling to some of the most remote and inhospitable coastlines on Earth, Abelsnes has photographed a landscape that exists almost entirely outside of human time. The ice in these images began forming millions of years ago, while Homo sapiens have only existed for roughly 300,000 years. Defined by such a scale, Antarctica is less a place than a record — vast, indifferent, treacherous, and staggeringly beautiful, holding a kind of cosmic truth that Abelsnes says is more important now than ever before.

title: California Native Creations Art Show
location: Person Senior Wing, Finley Community Center
description:
September is the 17th Annual Pomo Honoring Month. On Monday, Sept. 14, the 6th California Native Creations Art Show opens Person Senior Wing, Finley Community Center, 2060 W. College Ave., Santa Rosa, CA. The show is free and open to the public Monday – Friday, 8:30 a.m.-4:30 p.m., through November 19.

The established and up-and-coming native artists create with digital media, paint and traditional materials in their art, weaving, regalia, beadwork, jewelry, baskets and quilts. The artists include:

·         Meyo Marrufo, painter, guest curator for the de Young Museum and the Sonoma Valley Art Museum,

·         Buffie Campbell, Vice Chair, Sherwood Valley Rancheria, cultural teacher and master basket maker,

·         Henry Edward Frank, Yurok/Kashaya Pomo, who will show paintings and work with Legos titled Mind Prison,

·         Digital artist Nicolas \(Nico\) Vargas, Kashia Band of Pomo Indians, whose art was featured at the 55th Annual Stanford Powwow.

·         plus Gloria Carretero; Rose Hammock; Rudy Hammock; Jocelyn Garcia; Arella Ortega LaRose, Kashia Band of Pomo Indians; Angelica Smith, Manchester Point Arena and Yokayo Rancheria; Maria Pasalo; Michelle Napoli; Martina Morgan, Kashia Band of Pomo Indians; Hands Lopez; Shashoni Hanover-Redenbaugh; Katie Williams-Elliott, Juan Partida, and Mia Pasalo, Big Valley Pomo Tribe.

**Talasana Krama (Foundational Sequence) & Pranayama**

Fundamental practices for understanding the holistic nature, energetics and Sanskrit yoga philosophy guiding the approach of this comprehensive system. Long time yoga practitioners as well as new students will benefit. Experience the distinction of this system verses other modern yoga/vinyasa practices commonly taught & the traditional & precise use of ujjayi breath as it relates to the Sanskrit parameters, moving with the breath and the importance of the pause. Talasana is a very unique & profound krama initiating & establishing "samasthiti", the steadiness and focus of mind, balanced energy and steadiness of body - with the two feet together, moving from the center, all the major joints and muscles of the body are exercised using arm and hand movements, back bends, side bends, twists, forward bends, squats and balancing foot stretches. The fingers interlaced create a prana circuit as they come together in the repetitive movement over the head. The breath specific movements stretch the diaphragm, psoas, massage the heart and internal organs, clear the lungs, drain the lymphatic system, stimulate the vagus nerve and calm the mind. Energy is created along the spine and central nervous system, and is distributed throughout the nadis and into the entire energy body. Regular practice of Talasana flowers into to ananta samapatti and understanding "stillness in movement".
Class begins with Opening Mantras & Ding Namaskar (Devotional Salutation to the Directional Spheres with Breath & Mantra). Then moves to Tāĺāsana to Savasana then Seated Prānāyāma (Yogic Breathing) including Morning Cleansing Kriyas, Ujjayi, Nadi Shuddi, Samantraka Prānāyāma, Pratyahara, Dharana. title: Dia de Muertos at Jack London State Historic Park
description:
In recognition of Día de Muertos, Jack London State Historic Park will present two ofrendas in the House of Happy Walls Museum from Oct. 4 to Nov. 6, 2026.

Dia de Muertos, or Day of the Dead, is a tradition that began in Mexican and other Latino cultures.  An ofrenda, Spanish for ‘offering,’ is an altar created to honor and welcome the memory of those who have died.

The Legacy Ofrenda will honor writer and adventurer Jack London, Charmian London, and other individuals connected to the history of the property. Through photographs, reproductions, traditional elements of an ofrenda, and carefully selected symbolic objects, the installation will reflect Jack and Charmian's partnership, writing and travels, their life at Beauty Ranch, their connection to the land, and the legacies they left behind.

The Community Ofrenda will be a shared, participatory offering. Visitors, locals, volunteers, Board members, and employees can contribute a small photograph, written name, memory, drawing or message honoring someone who has passed away – including a beloved pet. 

The installation will grow throughout October as more people participate.  Materials will be available at the display for visitors who would like to join the celebration and contribute a name, memory or even a drawing of their loved one.

title: EAMES & EAMES: Meet the couple who Defined Modern Design
location: The MAC - Napa Valley Museum of Art & Culture
description:
EAMES & EAMES: Meet the couple who Defined Modern Design

Created in collaboration with the Eames Institute of Infinite Curiosity.

EAMES & EAMES explores the iterative, hands-on, and human-centered approach of Charles & Ray Eames. Through furniture, toys, paintings, graphics, and personal belongings collected over their lifetimes, this groundbreaking exhibition looks beyond the iconic Eames chairs to reveal the breadth of their creative practice. More than any single object, their work opened doors to new and unexpected ways of seeing, thinking, making, and understanding the world—ideas that continue to inspire us today.

Curated by Llisa Demetrios, Co-Founder & The Lucia Eames Chief Curator of the Eames Institute of Infinite Curiosity.

title: Maple Magic & Winter Wonder
description:
As the days grow shorter and cooler, Sonoma Botanical Garden transforms with the beauty of the changing seasons. From the first signs of autumn in October to the brilliant display of rare Asian maples in November and the quiet beauty of early winter in December, each visit offers something new to discover. 

Maple Magic & Winter Wonder invites visitors to experience this special time of year through nature, creativity, and connection. Throughout the season, the Garden offers guided walks, hands-on workshops, lectures, and special experiences inspired by the changing landscape. Wander among vibrant fall foliage, breathe in the sweet fragrance of katsura trees, enjoy creative programs, and experience the peaceful beauty of the Garden as it transitions into winter.

title: Art Exhibit: Aspirations
description:
Date: FOR IMMEDIATE RELEASE  9/15/26

**OCTOBER EXHIBIT: ASPIRATIONS**

EXHIBIT DATES **– September 28 – October 25, 2026**

**RECEPTION: SATURDAY, October 3, 2026, 3-6 pm: Join us to meet Laura Roney and Linda Loveland Reid and learn about their art and inspiration.  Be sure to take part in the Gallery’s free monthlong drawing for a beautiful work by a Gallery artist.  Refreshments will be served.**

Sonoma County artist, **Laura Roney,** unveils **Aspirations**, a new collection of paintings in oil, celebrating the unique differing goals people set during our lives, challenging us to take bold steps forward.  Of universal inspiration**, Aspiration and Awe** splashes the Milky Way’s starry brilliance across the heavens, capturing our imagination and hope as worldly cares are left behind.  Moving from natural forces to human endeavor, looking toward social change, **Aspiring to Vote**, the portrait of a hopeful suffragette, evokes the dream for a better future.  A lifetime goal for many, the marathon, **Aspiring for 26.2,** captures the early morning excitement waiting for start times.  “People doing ordinary things but dreaming larger for the future has been a great inspiration for this series.  I hope folks will be inspired by the boldness of people’s dreams,” commented Roney on her inspiration for the work.

Art has been a lifelong passion for Roney.  Beginning her art studies at a young age, whatever avenue she was pursuing in life, she continued her artistic endeavors.  After a successful career in microbiology and pharmaceutical research, a family move to Northern California enabled Roney to focus on her art.  She received her MFA from Academy of Art University, San Francisco.

Meet the artist: Roney will host the Gallery on September 30 and October 1 from 11am to 6 pm.

The Stairway Smallworks Showcase features Linda Loveland Reid’s **Intentional Chaos,** a collection of exciting mixed-media works that explode with excitement and energy. Random patterns, amorphous shapes and dancing dribbles magically coalesce into bold statements.  Intriguing and compelling, like interlocking gears, in **Patterns of Memory** multiple patterns interlock on fields of gold and black.  “I love throwing ink, paint and even coffee onto a blank canvas and creating through instinct, gesture and emotion.  Distilling energy into smaller works brings new challenges and some happy surprises,” noted Reid on her creative process.

Meet the artist: Reid will host the Gallery on October 23 from 11am to 6 pm.

 Also join us for **ART NITE HEALDSBURG**, Thursday, October 1, 5 – 7 pm.  ART NITE Healdsburg, held the 1st Thursday of Every Month, is a community event celebrating art and creativity with over 20 galleries participating.  ArtNiteHealdsburg.com.

title: Art Exhibit: Endless Inspiration
description:
Date: FOR IMMEDIATE RELEASE  10/12/26

**NOVEMBER EXHIBIT: ENDLESS INSPIRATION**

EXHIBIT DATES **– October 26  – November 22, 2026**

**RECEPTION: SATURDAY, November 7, 2026, 3-6 pm: Join us to meet Ron Sumner and Karen Miller and learn about their art and inspiration.  Be sure to take part in the Gallery’s free monthlong drawing for a beautiful work by a Gallery artist.  Refreshments will be served.**

Sonoma County artist, **Ron Sumner,** presents **Endless Inspiration**, a collection of new paintings and classic works that highlight his lifelong love of nature featuring landscapes, animals and wildlife, with a special focus on birds.  The essence of this golden state shines forth in “California Hills,” a large oil painting of a sweep of oak covered hills.   Turning to wildlife, Sumner’s masterful watercolor rendition in the “Young Fox” captures its wild nature on stark alert.  And the compelling presence of a most majestic bird is beautifully memorialized in his “Blue Heron” watercolor.  Other birds depicted in his works include parrots, penguins and owls.  “In my painting, I always strive to translate my emotional response to the world of nature around us – to share this deep feeling with those who view my work,” commented Sumner on his inspiration.

A lifelong Northern Californian, Sumner began his art training in school.  After earning a BFA from the California College of Arts & Crafts, he was a technical illustrator for a number of years before transitioning to a full-time fine arts painter.  With an emphasis in watercolor, he has won numerous awards, including Best of Show at the Society of Western Artists.  His portrait of John F. Kennedy is part of the permanent collection at the John F. Kennedy Library.  He has exhibited widely and was part of the Veterans Art Show for CA vets in 2023.

Meet the artist: Sumner will co-host Art Nite on 11/5 from 5 pm to 7 pm.

The Stairway Smallworks Showcase features **Karen Miller’**s **Historic Gems,** featuring pastel paintings that honor our history – local artifacts that are disappearing.  Highlighting this exhibit, “Ghost Bridge,” an early 20th century railroad bridge known as Healdsburg Railroad Bridge is soon to give way for the Smart Train.  Its unique style is a key element to our local character but sadly could not be upgraded for modern rail.  From old trucks to a beloved schoolhouse, these paintings harken fond memories.  Part of our world for years, they enriched our lives and are not to be forgotten.  Noted Miller on the impetus for her series, “I want to catch old things before they’re gone – memorializing those things close to our hearts.”

Meet the artist: Miller will host the Gallery on October 26 and November 2, 11, 14 & 15 from 11am to 2:30 pm.

 Also join us for **ART NITE HEALDSBURG**, Thursday, November 5, 5 – 7 pm.  ART NITE Healdsburg, held the 1st Thursday of Every Month, is a community event celebrating art and creativity with over 20 galleries participating.  ArtNiteHealdsburg.com.

For further information: Contact: Beverly Bird, Press Contact, at bvdrio@sonic.net or 707-799-1490.

title: Haunted Wine Tour & Tasting
description:
This fall, Buena Vista Winery invites you to uncover the mysteries, legends, and ghostly encounters woven into more than 165 years of history. Led by Sonoma historian and actor George Webber, this immersive 90 minute experience journeys through the historic Press House and Champagne Cellars, revealing true tales of unexplained happenings reported by Buena Vista team members and visitors throughout the years.

Hear the stories of the Glowing Ghostly Shirt, the Little Girl Who Says Hi, the mysterious Ghost Party on the Second Floor, the Old Man Who Walked Into a Stone Wall, and other strange occurrences that continue to add to the legend of Buena Vista.

Along the way, explore some of the winery’s most intriguing spaces, including the Bubble Lounge, Cave of Curiosities, and Wine Tool Museum, while enjoying five Buena Vista wines tasted throughout the experience, including a taste drawn directly from barrel.

And, as with any journey through Buena Vista’s extraordinary past, you never quite know when the winery’s legendary founder, Count Agoston Haraszthy, may choose to make an appearance.

History, wine, mystery, and perhaps a spirit or two await.

title: Salsa Beginners 2 - Mondays
description:
Ready to take your salsa to the next level? Salsa lessons in Marin will help you to add some flair and fluidity to your salsa dancing.

Pre-requisite: Salsa Beginners 1 – You know your basic steps, left turn, right turn, cross-body lead, and you hold your frame.

What You’ll Learn

We’ve curated a curriculum designed to build your confidence and your “social dance” vocabulary:

• The Cross Body Lead \(CBL\) Series: Master both Inside and Outside Turns, the essential building blocks for moving your partner across the floor with grace.

• The “I Turn – You Turn”: A classic social dance staple that develops timing and hand-change coordination.

• The Walk-Through: Learn how to transition smoothly through the dance space without breaking your rhythm.

• Footwork & Shine: We’ll break down the footwork pattern that adds personality to your “shines.”

Technique & Artistry

• Dancing is about more than just where your feet go. In this level, we dive deeper into the “how”:

• The Frame: Understand the “tension and compression” needed to lead and follow clearly without using muscle.

• Upper Body Mechanics: Learn how to isolate your ribcage and shoulders to move with that authentic Latin soul.

• Connection: Developing a “heavy” but responsive arm connection to ensure your partner feels every lead.

Important Details

• No dance experience required: Whether you’ve never danced before or it’s been a while, you’re welcome here!

• No partner necessary: Come solo or bring a friend—either way, you’ll have plenty of opportunities to dance.

• Please wear non-marking shoe soles: This helps us keep our dance floor in great condition.

title: Charlie Ginsburgh to present at the Napa Valley Photographic Society
description:
Please join fellow photography enthusiasts for Charlie Ginsburgh’s presentation on what makes a good photography image.

Charlie Ginsburgh has been involved in photography since 2011. In reflecting on his personal photographic style, Charlie states, “I find that I am attracted to the idea of ‘making the commonplace, uncommon’ in the world around me and especially in nature. I can be in a group of people overlooking a truly magnificent panoramic vista, and darn if I am not most interested in the little weedy flower-thing nearly buried in the dust at my feet.” 

Charlie has been involved in offering image commentary for the last seven years, offering commentary to over 250 SF Bay Area camera club and PSA affiliated clubs events.

He is currently both a Northern California Council of Camera Clubs \(N4C\) and Photographic Society of America \(PSA\) Photography judge and has participated in photographic competitions domestically throughout the Chicago / San Francisco Bay areas and internationally for PSA. Charlie has also been a speaker at the last four N4C Fotoclave conferences. He has also provided programs for local camera clubs on Action Photography, Macro Photography, Flower Photography, and Compositing / Photoshop editing. Charlie is currently the N4C Judges Chair, a past President of the Peninsula Camera Club in San Mateo, CA, and is an N4C Fellow.  Charlie will critique member-submitted photos after his presentation. 

Examples of his photography are provided on his web site \(https://charlie-g.smugmug.com\) and he can be reached via E-mail at cginsburgh@gmail.com

Napa Valley Photographic Society \(NVPS\) promotes the art and science of photography, providing education, image appreciation, inspiration, and exchange of technologies. Most months, we invite guest speakers to evaluate our images.  Guests are welcome to attend.  Check the website for more information: http://www.napavalleyphotographicsociety.org.
