title: Coordinated Entry Advisory Committee Meeting November 4, 2026
S.R. Laws
description:
S.R. LAWS IS OUT THERE: He approaches songwriting with a passion for songs that we all grew up on. His sound rings a familiar bell in your head while still delivering ideas completely unique.  He draws inspiration from outstanding storytellers like John Hiatt, Lou Reed, Steve Earle, Neil Finn and Ron Sexsmith. All of their music and others have carved a deep groove. 

Growing up out there in Northern California, he developed a unique connection to music early on. His father worked as a trash collector, and he would spend hours sifting through bags of discarded 45 records. Each find felt like stumbling upon hidden treasures. Some records were covered in dirt and grime, while others were pristine. The thrill of discovering new sounds was exhilarating, and he could hardly wait to drop the needle and immerse himself in the music.

He embarked on a pilgrimage to Texas with just two suitcases and $500 in his bank account. His goal was to dive into the vibrant music scene and learn from fellow songwriters. Austin, known as the "Live Music Capital of the World," offered countless opportunities for him to grow as an artist. Open mics and songwriters' nights became his training ground, where he soaked up every moment, listening to others share their stories through music.

These days, he resides in Sonoma County, California, working hard as a touring artist and singer-songwriter for his original rock band, The Heartsleeves. He invites everyone to join him on this musical journey, sharing his songs one person at a time in this vast and unpredictable world we live in.

“Scott Ray Laws is an unique and really cool songwriter…he digs into materials, tells a story in his songs, and has a clean baritone vocality that is easy on the ears. We had a chance to meet and hang with Scott back in May ..and I HAD to have him back for a Wednesday evening.” Luigi- Owner-The Listening Room.

“..An ORIGINAL songwriter who knows how to tell a story clearly in song” -  Scotty O’Neill - Guitarist/Promoter

“ It was such a treat catching your set last night — really refreshing to hear something new and original. Thanks for pulling up a chair and hanging out with us — we really enjoyed the conversation and the stories behind your songs.”  -Tripp B. - Sonoma Songwriter

“Expect slow burning passion and vivid music …the kind of energy that turns into “let’s stay for just one more!..”  - Doug- Owner/Wine Maker- Spicy Vines

“...His lyrics simply tell first-person stories from his own life. Nothing fancy, he's not writing to impress--he pours himself, as is, into each phrase and melody.”- Rebecca Roudman- Dirty Cello Radio Hour KRCB Radio 104.9 FM

“ It is through forthright lyrics that are personal and earnest, that he composes lyrical pictures. Taking snapshots from the most common walks of life...”  - David Sampson - Producer Studio Secti West

“..relaxed mid-tempo Americana, capturing in each song the rhythmic pocket Laws is known for creating.” -  Coyote Music Review 2024

title: Napa Primary Care Conference November 4-8, 2026
description:
The Napa Primary Care Conference is a unique educational conference for physicians and medical professionals who care for active and athletic patients or who themselves lead such a lifestyle.

16 HOURS AAFP CME CREDIT

Location

The conference will be held at The Napa Valley Marriott Resort and Spa, conveniently located within minutes of renowned wineries, shopping, attractions, and numerous options for exercise and physical activity.

Course Description

This conference will present very practical information that you can use in your practice. Topics will include common medical and musculoskeletal problems that affect patients who lead an active lifestyle. The focus will be on providing information that will help you diagnose and manage these conditions in the office; so that you can help your patients get moving again and improve their performance. In addition, various topics on healthy lifestyles and personal wellness will make this conference a valuable experience for all attendees.

Intended Audience

The curriculum is directed to Family Medicine, Internal Medicine, Pediatrics, Emergency Medicine, PM and R and Orthopedics specialists as well as Physical Therapists, Athletic Trainers, Physicians Assistants, Nurse Practitioners and others who want to earn Continuing Medical Education from leading physician experts who are outstanding speakers.

Course Learning Objectives

Upon conclusion of this program, participants should be able to:

1. Describe recent advances regarding various medical problems and their impact on the athlete and exercise performance.

2. Identify current recommendations for proper nutrition in active and athletic patients.

3. Illustrate key skills in the diagnosis and management of common musculoskeletal problems encountered by family physicians.

4. Diagnose common problems encountered by patients and effectively treat these conditions.

5. Define common medical-legal issues relevant to the primary care physician.

We hope you can join us for this unique conference in 2024. I look forward to meeting you in Napa!

Sincerely,

Robert Sallis, MD, FACSM, FAAFP

After his college experience at California College of Arts and Crafts with Viola Frey and further work at Humboldt State University with Lew Merrick, he ran a stained glass business for 18 years. Michael and his wife left for Turkey in 1991 to teach in International Schools. For 26 years he taught K-12 art, including Ceramics, Drawing, Photography, Design and Sculpture at schools in six different countries. He started clay programs for High School and Middle School students at three of those schools. At four of these schools he offered after school and weekend ceramics sessions for teachers and parents. Michael’s work ranges from the traditional to the experimental and a wide swath in between. His approach to teaching is to help students explore the playful nature of the clay room and nurture a love for the possibilities that medium presents.

title: Antarctica: The Frozen Desert | Photographs by Vegar Abelsnes
description:
1st Street Gallery at WTRSHD will present “Antarctica: The Frozen Desert,” a new body of fine art photography by Vegar Abelsnes, opening September 26th, 2026, and on view September through November.  The exhibition marks a deliberate turn in Abelsnes’ photography; after more than two decades of working in a commercial and advertising capacity, he has embarked on a career as a photo and field guide in the polar regions. The exhibit features work generated over 6 voyages to the Antarctic Peninsula. He is returning to Antarctica in January and will add the Falklands and South Georgia to his list of destinations to guide and photograph.

Traveling to some of the most remote and inhospitable coastlines on Earth, Abelsnes has photographed a landscape that exists almost entirely outside of human time. The ice in these images began forming millions of years ago, while Homo sapiens have only existed for roughly 300,000 years. Defined by such a scale, Antarctica is less a place than a record — vast, indifferent, treacherous, and staggeringly beautiful, holding a kind of cosmic truth that Abelsnes says is more important now than ever before.

title: Dia de Muertos at Jack London State Historic Park
description:
In recognition of Día de Muertos, Jack London State Historic Park will present two ofrendas in the House of Happy Walls Museum from Oct. 4 to Nov. 6, 2026.

Dia de Muertos, or Day of the Dead, is a tradition that began in Mexican and other Latino cultures.  An ofrenda, Spanish for ‘offering,’ is an altar created to honor and welcome the memory of those who have died.

The Legacy Ofrenda will honor writer and adventurer Jack London, Charmian London, and other individuals connected to the history of the property. Through photographs, reproductions, traditional elements of an ofrenda, and carefully selected symbolic objects, the installation will reflect Jack and Charmian's partnership, writing and travels, their life at Beauty Ranch, their connection to the land, and the legacies they left behind.

The Community Ofrenda will be a shared, participatory offering. Visitors, locals, volunteers, Board members, and employees can contribute a small photograph, written name, memory, drawing or message honoring someone who has passed away – including a beloved pet. 

The installation will grow throughout October as more people participate.  Materials will be available at the display for visitors who would like to join the celebration and contribute a name, memory or even a drawing of their loved one.

EAMES & EAMES explores the iterative, hands-on, and human-centered approach of Charles & Ray Eames. Through furniture, toys, paintings, graphics, and personal belongings collected over their lifetimes, this groundbreaking exhibition looks beyond the iconic Eames chairs to reveal the breadth of their creative practice. More than any single object, their work opened doors to new and unexpected ways of seeing, thinking, making, and understanding the world—ideas that continue to inspire us today.

Curated by Llisa Demetrios, Co-Founder & The Lucia Eames Chief Curator of the Eames Institute of Infinite Curiosity.

title: Art Exhibit: Aspirations
description:
Date: FOR IMMEDIATE RELEASE  9/15/26

**OCTOBER EXHIBIT: ASPIRATIONS**

EXHIBIT DATES **– September 28 – October 25, 2026**

**RECEPTION: SATURDAY, October 3, 2026, 3-6 pm: Join us to meet Laura Roney and Linda Loveland Reid and learn about their art and inspiration.  Be sure to take part in the Gallery’s free monthlong drawing for a beautiful work by a Gallery artist.  Refreshments will be served.**

Sonoma County artist, **Laura Roney,** unveils **Aspirations**, a new collection of paintings in oil, celebrating the unique differing goals people set during our lives, challenging us to take bold steps forward.  Of universal inspiration**, Aspiration and Awe** splashes the Milky Way’s starry brilliance across the heavens, capturing our imagination and hope as worldly cares are left behind.  Moving from natural forces to human endeavor, looking toward social change, **Aspiring to Vote**, the portrait of a hopeful suffragette, evokes the dream for a better future.  A lifetime goal for many, the marathon, **Aspiring for 26.2,** captures the early morning excitement waiting for start times.  “People doing ordinary things but dreaming larger for the future has been a great inspiration for this series.  I hope folks will be inspired by the boldness of people’s dreams,” commented Roney on her inspiration for the work.

Art has been a lifelong passion for Roney.  Beginning her art studies at a young age, whatever avenue she was pursuing in life, she continued her artistic endeavors.  After a successful career in microbiology and pharmaceutical research, a family move to Northern California enabled Roney to focus on her art.  She received her MFA from Academy of Art University, San Francisco.

Meet the artist: Roney will host the Gallery on September 30 and October 1 from 11am to 6 pm.

The Stairway Smallworks Showcase features Linda Loveland Reid’s **Intentional Chaos,** a collection of exciting mixed-media works that explode with excitement and energy. Random patterns, amorphous shapes and dancing dribbles magically coalesce into bold statements.  Intriguing and compelling, like interlocking gears, in **Patterns of Memory** multiple patterns interlock on fields of gold and black.  “I love throwing ink, paint and even coffee onto a blank canvas and creating through instinct, gesture and emotion.  Distilling energy into smaller works brings new challenges and some happy surprises,” noted Reid on her creative process.

Meet the artist: Reid will host the Gallery on October 23 from 11am to 6 pm.

 Also join us for **ART NITE HEALDSBURG**, Thursday, October 1, 5 – 7 pm.  ART NITE Healdsburg, held the 1st Thursday of Every Month, is a community event celebrating art and creativity with over 20 galleries participating.  ArtNiteHealdsburg.com.

For further information: Contact: Beverly Bird, Press Contact, at bvdrio@sonic.net or 707-799-1490.

title: Art Exhibit: Endless Inspiration
description:
Date: FOR IMMEDIATE RELEASE  10/12/26

**NOVEMBER EXHIBIT: ENDLESS INSPIRATION**

EXHIBIT DATES **– October 26  – November 22, 2026**

**RECEPTION: SATURDAY, November 7, 2026, 3-6 pm: Join us to meet Ron Sumner and Karen Miller and learn about their art and inspiration.  Be sure to take part in the Gallery’s free monthlong drawing for a beautiful work by a Gallery artist.  Refreshments will be served.**

Sonoma County artist, **Ron Sumner,** presents **Endless Inspiration**, a collection of new paintings and classic works that highlight his lifelong love of nature featuring landscapes, animals and wildlife, with a special focus on birds.  The essence of this golden state shines forth in “California Hills,” a large oil painting of a sweep of oak covered hills.   Turning to wildlife, Sumner’s masterful watercolor rendition in the “Young Fox” captures its wild nature on stark alert.  And the compelling presence of a most majestic bird is beautifully memorialized in his “Blue Heron” watercolor.  Other birds depicted in his works include parrots, penguins and owls.  “In my painting, I always strive to translate my emotional response to the world of nature around us – to share this deep feeling with those who view my work,” commented Sumner on his inspiration.

A lifelong Northern Californian, Sumner began his art training in school.  After earning a BFA from the California College of Arts & Crafts, he was a technical illustrator for a number of years before transitioning to a full-time fine arts painter.  With an emphasis in watercolor, he has won numerous awards, including Best of Show at the Society of Western Artists.  His portrait of John F. Kennedy is part of the permanent collection at the John F. Kennedy Library.  He has exhibited widely and was part of the Veterans Art Show for CA vets in 2023.

Meet the artist: Sumner will co-host Art Nite on 11/5 from 5 pm to 7 pm.

The Stairway Smallworks Showcase features **Karen Miller’**s **Historic Gems,** featuring pastel paintings that honor our history – local artifacts that are disappearing.  Highlighting this exhibit, “Ghost Bridge,” an early 20th century railroad bridge known as Healdsburg Railroad Bridge is soon to give way for the Smart Train.  Its unique style is a key element to our local character but sadly could not be upgraded for modern rail.  From old trucks to a beloved schoolhouse, these paintings harken fond memories.  Part of our world for years, they enriched our lives and are not to be forgotten.  Noted Miller on the impetus for her series, “I want to catch old things before they’re gone – memorializing those things close to our hearts.”

Meet the artist: Miller will host the Gallery on October 26 and November 2, 11, 14 & 15 from 11am to 2:30 pm.

 Also join us for **ART NITE HEALDSBURG**, Thursday, November 5, 5 – 7 pm.  ART NITE Healdsburg, held the 1st Thursday of Every Month, is a community event celebrating art and creativity with over 20 galleries participating.  ArtNiteHealdsburg.com.

title: Lost Canadians, Border Crossings, and Citizenship by Descent (Speaker Series)
description: Kathryn Lake Hogan Hailing from Southwestern Ontario, Kathryn's lineage includes a mixture of Canadian, Loyalist and New England branches and roots connecting her to England and Wales. But her passion doesn't stop at her own genealogy; Kathryn's mission is to help others discover their Canadian ancestral connections. Kathryn's dynamic presentations, ranging from society meetings to genealogical research institutes in Canada and the United States, have earned her a reputation as one of the leading voices in Canadian genealogy. Whether you've attended one of her sessions or tuned into her "Genealogy with a Canadian Twist" webinars, you've likely felt the excitement of Kathryn's dedication. Kathryn's commitment goes beyond her business. She believes in nurturing and growing the genealogy community. Having served in leadership roles for notable organizations such as Ontario Ancestors, the Association of Professional Genealogists, and the United Empire Loyalists Association of Canada, she continues to champion greater accessibility, inclusivity, and diversity in family history. title: Napa Primary Care Conference November 4-8, 2026
description:
The Napa Primary Care Conference is a unique educational conference for physicians and medical professionals who care for active and athletic patients or who themselves lead such a lifestyle.

16 HOURS AAFP CME CREDIT

Location

The conference will be held at The Napa Valley Marriott Resort and Spa, conveniently located within minutes of renowned wineries, shopping, attractions, and numerous options for exercise and physical activity.

Course Description

This conference will present very practical information that you can use in your practice. Topics will include common medical and musculoskeletal problems that affect patients who lead an active lifestyle. The focus will be on providing information that will help you diagnose and manage these conditions in the office; so that you can help your patients get moving again and improve their performance. In addition, various topics on healthy lifestyles and personal wellness will make this conference a valuable experience for all attendees.

Intended Audience

The curriculum is directed to Family Medicine, Internal Medicine, Pediatrics, Emergency Medicine, PM and R and Orthopedics specialists as well as Physical Therapists, Athletic Trainers, Physicians Assistants, Nurse Practitioners and others who want to earn Continuing Medical Education from leading physician experts who are outstanding speakers.

Course Learning Objectives

Upon conclusion of this program, participants should be able to:

1. Describe recent advances regarding various medical problems and their impact on the athlete and exercise performance.

2. Identify current recommendations for proper nutrition in active and athletic patients.

3. Illustrate key skills in the diagnosis and management of common musculoskeletal problems encountered by family physicians.

4. Diagnose common problems encountered by patients and effectively treat these conditions.

5. Define common medical-legal issues relevant to the primary care physician.

We hope you can join us for this unique conference in 2024. I look forward to meeting you in Napa!

Sincerely,

Robert Sallis, MD, FACSM, FAAFP

title: Belly Dancing with Raja - Thursdays
description:
DATE AND TIME: Thursdays, 5:30 PM

Unlock your inner strength and find your flow. Belly dancing with Raja is an innovative fusion class that blends the rhythmic artistry of belly dance with the high-energy benefits of aerobics. Designed to be both a cardiovascular challenge and a deep toning session, this class focuses on the “powerhouse” of the body—your core.

By layering fluid, isolative movements over an athletic aerobic base, you will challenge your muscles in ways traditional gym workouts can’t reach.

What to Expect in Belly Dancing Class

• Core-Centric Power: Use undulations and shimmies to engage deep abdominal muscles for a tighter, stronger midsection.

• Functional Stability: Improve your balance and posture through controlled, hip-driven movements and low-impact aerobic footwork.

• Total Body Toning: Build lean muscle in your legs, glutes, and arms while maintaining a constant, heart-pumping pace.

• Mind-Body Connection: Enhance your coordination and body awareness through rhythmic, expressive choreography.

“Whether you’re looking to define your waistline or simply want a workout that feels like a celebration, this class offers the perfect balance of sweat and grace.”

Difficulty Level: All levels welcome! No prior dance experience is required—just bring your energy and a willingness to move.

title: Bachata Beginners Thursday
description:
Your First Steps into Bachata

This class is perfect for bachata beginners that want to learn basic steps and skills, or those who want to refresh their foundational skills. We understand that learning something new can feel a little intimidating. That’s why our supportive and relaxed environment is specifically designed to make learning bachata basics an absolute blast!

Our friendly instructors will guide you through:

**Basic directional steps:** You’ll learn the fundamental movements that form the building blocks of all bachata dancing.

**Proper frame for partner work:** Discover how to connect comfortably and effectively with a partner, setting you up for smooth and enjoyable dances.

**Simple turn patterns:** We’ll introduce you to easy-to-follow turn patterns that will have you dancing with a partner in no time.

We’ve carefully organized our curriculum to ensure that each movement is easy to grasp and remember, building your confidence with every step. Our goal is to make learning fun. Join us to learn Bachata in Marin.

Important Details

**No dance experience required:** Whether you’ve never danced before or it’s been a while, you’re welcome here!

**No partner necessary:** Come solo or bring a friend—either way, you’ll have plenty of opportunities to dance.

Please wear **non-marking shoe soles:** This helps us keep our dance floor in great condition.

Come join us and discover the joy of bachata! We can’t wait to see you on the dance floor.

Get ready to feel the rhythm and energy of Rio de Janeiro! **Samba no Pé** (Samba in the Foot) is the captivating solo style of samba danced in the streets and at Carnival, known for its rapid, intricate footwork and infectious hip movements.

**You will learn**

The Basic Step: You will master the signature quick-quick-slow rhythm that defines Samba no Pé.

Arm & Hip Styling: You will learn how to add the authentic flair, movement, and energy that makes Brazilian samba so captivating.

Technique & Posture: You will receive tips on proper body alignment to help you dance longer, faster, and more safely.

Rhythm & Musicality: You will learn how to connect your movement directly to the irresistible beat of the bateria (the samba drum section).

This class is perfect for anyone looking to connect with the vibrant spirit of Brazil, improve coordination, and get a fantastic workout—all while learning the foundational steps of this iconic dance. No partner or prior dance experience is required! Just bring your enthusiasm and comfortable shoes!

Date & Time: Thursdays @6:30PM – 7:30PM

Address: 4140 Redwood Highway #8 San Rafael, CA

Note: Arrive 10 minutes before. No floor marking shoe soles allowed.

title: True West
description: Set in a suburban California home, True West follows two brothers with sharply contrasting personalities who reunite while house-sitting for their mother. One is a disciplined, aspiring screenwriter, while the other lives a more nomadic and unpredictable life. As they reconnect, their interactions shift from uneasy familiarity to intense competition, fueled by conflicting ambitions and long-standing tensions. Shepard's play delves into themes of authenticity, creativity, and the myth of the American frontier, using sharp dialogue and dark humor to reveal the instability beneath the surface of everyday life. As the brothers' dynamic evolves, the boundaries between their identities begin to blur, raising questions about who they are and what defines them.

title: Bennett Friedman Jazz Quartet
description: The concert will feature guitarist Randy Vincent, bassist Robb Fisher, drummer Kendrick Freeman, and saxophonist Bennett Friedman.Randy Vincent has been teaching jazz guitar at Sonoma State University since 1981. He has performed with Bobby Hutcherson, Joe Henderson, and Dizzy Gillespie. Vincent has authored six jazz guitar books, published by Sher Music Co.  Bassist Robb Fisher toured and recorded with the legendary Cal Tjader for more than six years, anchoring Tjader's Grammy Award-winning album, "La Onda Va Bien," and Grammy-nominated album, "Gozame Pero Ya." He has also worked extensively with and recorded for jazz and Latin artists, including Chet Baker, Art Pepper, Carmen McRae, Tania Mara, Clare Fischer, Rob Schneiderman, Eddie Marshall, Dick Whittington, and Anita O'Day.Kendrick Freeman has a background in both drum set and hand drums, having studied with American artists and musicians from Ghana, Congo, and the Caribbean, with an emphasis on Haitian music. Freeman leads a jazz ensemble at Sonoma State University.  Saxophonist Bennett Friedman has performed at the Monterey Jazz Festival, the Stanford Jazz Workshop, the San Jose Jazz Festival, the Healdsburg Jazz Festival, the Monterey Bay Blues Festival, and the Russian River Jazz Festival. He has been featured as a soloist with Frank Sinatra, Rosemary Clooney, Natalie Cole, and Marvin Gaye. Friedman has taught Jazz Studies at Santa Rosa Junior College since 1977. He is the recipient of a National Endowment for the Arts grant for jazz composition.  Concert proceeds benefit the SRJC Foundation Jazz Studies Fund. title: Gain Speaking Confidence with Mare Island Toastmasters
description:
We meet in-person only on the 1st and 2nd Thursdays of the month. However, you can catch us online every Thursday unless the meeting date falls on a holiday.

Please register at https://signup.com/go/WiniixA

What is Toastmasters About?

Usually at our meetings, we will have a prepared speech, and a speech evaluation. The Grammarian and Wizard of Ah's will listen for turns of phrases and the use of filler words. We also practice impromptu speaking during the section of the meeting called Table Topics. During Table Topics, at a recent meeting, we were asked what we felt was the biggest communication problem or challenge. What would you answer in a fast moment? Table topics will challenge you to think quickly and give an answer without preparation.

You will also hear tips on public speaking skills at our upcoming meeting. Whether you're a seasoned traveler or just looking for some adventure from the comfort of your home, this event is perfect for you.

Toastmasters International is all about communication excellence, and for 100 years and counting, Toastmasters have been expressing themselves better, practicing, and evaluating in a fun club environment, shining all around the world.

To find out more--Msg us on our webpage \(under Contact Us\) button at

https://mareisland.toastmastersclubs.org/

If you will join us in-person on the first or second Thursday of the month, we meet this week at Kaiser Hospital Bldg. A. 3rd floor meeting room. title: Jizo Peace Project: Clay Gathering for Remembrance and Peace, November — Sebastopol Center For the Arts, California
location: Sebastopol Center for the Arts, 282 S High St, Sebastopol, CA 95472
description:
Jizo Peace Project: Clay Gathering for Remembrance and Peace, November

  
    
      
        
          $10.00
        
      
    
  

Friday, November 6, 2026; 1:30 – 4:00pmDue to limited capacity, we are asking for a suggested donation of $10 to the Sebastopol Center for the Arts to confirm your attendance. Bring a copy of your receipt at check-in to Painting/Drawing Studio adjacent to Ceramics Studio. Additional donations are welcome at the time of the class to cover rental and expenses for the peace project. Join us for a monthly, heart-centered gathering where we come together to create Jizo guardians out of clay—symbols of compassion, protection, and peace. Rooted in the Buddhist tradition and echoed across many cultures, Jizo figures traditionally honor children and all who have passed, those in transition, and those in distress.This ongoing project is dedicated to remembering those lost to war, with a special focus now on the approximately 19,000 children who have perished in Israel and Gaza in recent years. Through the simple, meditative act of working with clay, we create benevolent beings that will become part of public exhibits and peace sites, offering spaces for reflection, mourning, and hope. Our gatherings conclude with a gentle ritual to honor the lives of these children.Located in the Painting & Drawing Room. The gathering is open to ages 12 - adult, and no prior clay experience is necessary—all clay and basic materials are supplied. Registration is required to participate.Donations are welcome to help cover materials and expenses. More than a class, this is a shared space of warmth and care—an opportunity to tend to our own hearts while taking part in love in action.

title: Antarctica: The Frozen Desert | Photographs by Vegar Abelsnes
description:
1st Street Gallery at WTRSHD will present “Antarctica: The Frozen Desert,” a new body of fine art photography by Vegar Abelsnes, opening September 26th, 2026, and on view September through November.  The exhibition marks a deliberate turn in Abelsnes’ photography; after more than two decades of working in a commercial and advertising capacity, he has embarked on a career as a photo and field guide in the polar regions. The exhibit features work generated over 6 voyages to the Antarctic Peninsula. He is returning to Antarctica in January and will add the Falklands and South Georgia to his list of destinations to guide and photograph.

Traveling to some of the most remote and inhospitable coastlines on Earth, Abelsnes has photographed a landscape that exists almost entirely outside of human time. The ice in these images began forming millions of years ago, while Homo sapiens have only existed for roughly 300,000 years. Defined by such a scale, Antarctica is less a place than a record — vast, indifferent, treacherous, and staggeringly beautiful, holding a kind of cosmic truth that Abelsnes says is more important now than ever before.

·         Buffie Campbell, Vice Chair, Sherwood Valley Rancheria, cultural teacher and master basket maker,

·         Henry Edward Frank, Yurok/Kashaya Pomo, who will show paintings and work with Legos titled Mind Prison,

·         Digital artist Nicolas \(Nico\) Vargas, Kashia Band of Pomo Indians, whose art was featured at the 55th Annual Stanford Powwow.

·         plus Gloria Carretero; Rose Hammock; Rudy Hammock; Jocelyn Garcia; Arella Ortega LaRose, Kashia Band of Pomo Indians; Angelica Smith, Manchester Point Arena and Yokayo Rancheria; Maria Pasalo; Michelle Napoli; Martina Morgan, Kashia Band of Pomo Indians; Hands Lopez; Shashoni Hanover-Redenbaugh; Katie Williams-Elliott, Juan Partida, and Mia Pasalo, Big Valley Pomo Tribe.

title: Dia de Muertos at Jack London State Historic Park
description:
In recognition of Día de Muertos, Jack London State Historic Park will present two ofrendas in the House of Happy Walls Museum from Oct. 4 to Nov. 6, 2026.

Dia de Muertos, or Day of the Dead, is a tradition that began in Mexican and other Latino cultures.  An ofrenda, Spanish for ‘offering,’ is an altar created to honor and welcome the memory of those who have died.

The Legacy Ofrenda will honor writer and adventurer Jack London, Charmian London, and other individuals connected to the history of the property. Through photographs, reproductions, traditional elements of an ofrenda, and carefully selected symbolic objects, the installation will reflect Jack and Charmian's partnership, writing and travels, their life at Beauty Ranch, their connection to the land, and the legacies they left behind.

The Community Ofrenda will be a shared, participatory offering. Visitors, locals, volunteers, Board members, and employees can contribute a small photograph, written name, memory, drawing or message honoring someone who has passed away – including a beloved pet. 

The installation will grow throughout October as more people participate.  Materials will be available at the display for visitors who would like to join the celebration and contribute a name, memory or even a drawing of their loved one.

EAMES & EAMES: Meet the couple who Defined Modern Design

Created in collaboration with the Eames Institute of Infinite Curiosity.

EAMES & EAMES explores the iterative, hands-on, and human-centered approach of Charles & Ray Eames. Through furniture, toys, paintings, graphics, and personal belongings collected over their lifetimes, this groundbreaking exhibition looks beyond the iconic Eames chairs to reveal the breadth of their creative practice. More than any single object, their work opened doors to new and unexpected ways of seeing, thinking, making, and understanding the world—ideas that continue to inspire us today.

Curated by Llisa Demetrios, Co-Founder & The Lucia Eames Chief Curator of the Eames Institute of Infinite Curiosity.

description:
Marin Arts & Crafts Show returns to the Marin Center Exhibit Hall November 6–8, filling the hall with more than 200 exhibits of fine craft, art and artisan goods. Arriving just as the holiday season gets underway, the three-day market brings together an exciting mix of artists, artisans and craftspeople for a weekend of art, handcraft and seasonal discoveries.

Inspired by the Arts & Crafts movement, the show celebrates craftsmanship, thoughtful design and artistic expression in its many forms. Visitors will find jewelry, ceramics, textiles, glass, woodwork, fine art, furniture, wearable art and specialty foods from artisan food makers. From hand-dyed silks and sculptural ceramics to finely crafted jewelry and heirloom-quality woodworking, the market brings together traditional techniques, fresh ideas and contemporary design.

Throughout the weekend, visitors can talk with artists about their work, watch demonstrations and explore the many forms of handcraft represented at the show. It's a chance to see the details up close, hear how things are made and get to know some of the people behind the work.

The November show brings a festive atmosphere to the Marin Center, with a bustling marketplace of fine crafts, art and artisan foods. Visitors can enjoy wine tasting, sample seasonal treats from specialty food merchants and listen to live music throughout the weekend. Free opportunity drawings offer chances to win wonderful prizes donated by participating artisans, adding to the excitement.

With free admission and free parking, Marin Arts & Crafts Show is an inviting way to spend a fall afternoon with family and friends. As the holidays approach, the market is also a wonderful place to discover distinctive gifts while supporting independent artisans.

title: "Hunting for the Snark Illustrations" with the Jack London Society
description:
Step inside the House of Happy Walls Museum for a fascinating exploration of Jack London’s photographic journey aboard the Snark with Professor Emerita Any Tucker.

Jack London always referred to The Cruise of the Snark \(1911\) as an “illustrated book.” The pictures were central to his authorial vision of the voyage to the South Pacific that he and Charmian London embarked on in April of 1907. Maddeningly, in the process of preparing the manuscript of The Cruise of the Snark for publication, Macmillan & Co. made a hash of the author’s design, misplacing some of the book’s 119 photographs and scrambling the captions Jack so carefully assembled.

Tucker explains, “While Jay Williams, my co-editor for Volume 13 of Oxford UP’s ‘Complete Works of Jack London,’ has been collating various iterations of the essays collected in ‘The Cruise of the Snark’ to prepare a definitive copy text, I’ve been trying to track down the original photographs for the book.  The treasure hunt has proved more challenging—and surprising—than expected. The pictures, most by Jack with a few by Martin Johnson, the Snark’s young cook and engineer, are scattered among far-flung sources—beginning with Charmian London’s huge collection of photo albums at the Huntington Library and multiple binders of prints and negatives housed in the California State Parks collection at Sonoma Barracks. My search eventually took me to archives in Chanute, Kansas; Auckland, NZ; and the British Museum, for it turns out that there was another, unacknowledged contributor to Jack’s illustrated book.”

About the speaker: Amy Tucker is Professor Emerita of the English Department of Queens College, CUNY, where she taught American literature and cultural studies. She has published essays on art, travel and literature, and served as guest editor of a volume on Charmian London for “Women’s Studies: An Inter-Disciplinary Journal.”  Her books include “The Illustration of the Master: Henry James and the Magazine Revolution;” “Visual Literacy: Writing about Art;” and, most recently, “I’m Used to Playing Lead: Memoirs by Women in Jazz,” to be brought out by Equinox in January, 2027. Tucker and Williams have received a two-year grant from the National Endowment for the Humanities to work on their volume for “The Complete Works of Jack London.”

This event is part of a speaker series co-hosted by Jack London Park Partners and the Jack London Society, honoring the 150th anniversary of Jack London’s birth. JLPP is grateful for the support of the Jack London Society and its scholars in bringing this speaker series to life. Join us at Jack London State Historic Park throughout 2026 for a compelling lineup of speakers celebrating Jack London’s legacy.  Learn more at https://jacklondonsociety.org/.

title: Art Exhibit: Aspirations
description:
Date: FOR IMMEDIATE RELEASE  9/15/26

**OCTOBER EXHIBIT: ASPIRATIONS**

EXHIBIT DATES **– September 28 – October 25, 2026**

**RECEPTION: SATURDAY, October 3, 2026, 3-6 pm: Join us to meet Laura Roney and Linda Loveland Reid and learn about their art and inspiration.  Be sure to take part in the Gallery’s free monthlong drawing for a beautiful work by a Gallery artist.  Refreshments will be served.**

Sonoma County artist, **Laura Roney,** unveils **Aspirations**, a new collection of paintings in oil, celebrating the unique differing goals people set during our lives, challenging us to take bold steps forward.  Of universal inspiration**, Aspiration and Awe** splashes the Milky Way’s starry brilliance across the heavens, capturing our imagination and hope as worldly cares are left behind.  Moving from natural forces to human endeavor, looking toward social change, **Aspiring to Vote**, the portrait of a hopeful suffragette, evokes the dream for a better future.  A lifetime goal for many, the marathon, **Aspiring for 26.2,** captures the early morning excitement waiting for start times.  “People doing ordinary things but dreaming larger for the future has been a great inspiration for this series.  I hope folks will be inspired by the boldness of people’s dreams,” commented Roney on her inspiration for the work.

Art has been a lifelong passion for Roney.  Beginning her art studies at a young age, whatever avenue she was pursuing in life, she continued her artistic endeavors.  After a successful career in microbiology and pharmaceutical research, a family move to Northern California enabled Roney to focus on her art.  She received her MFA from Academy of Art University, San Francisco.

Meet the artist: Roney will host the Gallery on September 30 and October 1 from 11am to 6 pm.

The Stairway Smallworks Showcase features Linda Loveland Reid’s **Intentional Chaos,** a collection of exciting mixed-media works that explode with excitement and energy. Random patterns, amorphous shapes and dancing dribbles magically coalesce into bold statements.  Intriguing and compelling, like interlocking gears, in **Patterns of Memory** multiple patterns interlock on fields of gold and black.  “I love throwing ink, paint and even coffee onto a blank canvas and creating through instinct, gesture and emotion.  Distilling energy into smaller works brings new challenges and some happy surprises,” noted Reid on her creative process.

Meet the artist: Reid will host the Gallery on October 23 from 11am to 6 pm.

 Also join us for **ART NITE HEALDSBURG**, Thursday, October 1, 5 – 7 pm.  ART NITE Healdsburg, held the 1st Thursday of Every Month, is a community event celebrating art and creativity with over 20 galleries participating.  ArtNiteHealdsburg.com.

title: Art Exhibit: Endless Inspiration
description:
Date: FOR IMMEDIATE RELEASE  10/12/26

**NOVEMBER EXHIBIT: ENDLESS INSPIRATION**

EXHIBIT DATES **– October 26  – November 22, 2026**

**RECEPTION: SATURDAY, November 7, 2026, 3-6 pm: Join us to meet Ron Sumner and Karen Miller and learn about their art and inspiration.  Be sure to take part in the Gallery’s free monthlong drawing for a beautiful work by a Gallery artist.  Refreshments will be served.**

Sonoma County artist, **Ron Sumner,** presents **Endless Inspiration**, a collection of new paintings and classic works that highlight his lifelong love of nature featuring landscapes, animals and wildlife, with a special focus on birds.  The essence of this golden state shines forth in “California Hills,” a large oil painting of a sweep of oak covered hills.   Turning to wildlife, Sumner’s masterful watercolor rendition in the “Young Fox” captures its wild nature on stark alert.  And the compelling presence of a most majestic bird is beautifully memorialized in his “Blue Heron” watercolor.  Other birds depicted in his works include parrots, penguins and owls.  “In my painting, I always strive to translate my emotional response to the world of nature around us – to share this deep feeling with those who view my work,” commented Sumner on his inspiration.

A lifelong Northern Californian, Sumner began his art training in school.  After earning a BFA from the California College of Arts & Crafts, he was a technical illustrator for a number of years before transitioning to a full-time fine arts painter.  With an emphasis in watercolor, he has won numerous awards, including Best of Show at the Society of Western Artists.  His portrait of John F. Kennedy is part of the permanent collection at the John F. Kennedy Library.  He has exhibited widely and was part of the Veterans Art Show for CA vets in 2023.

Meet the artist: Sumner will co-host Art Nite on 11/5 from 5 pm to 7 pm.

The Stairway Smallworks Showcase features **Karen Miller’**s **Historic Gems,** featuring pastel paintings that honor our history – local artifacts that are disappearing.  Highlighting this exhibit, “Ghost Bridge,” an early 20th century railroad bridge known as Healdsburg Railroad Bridge is soon to give way for the Smart Train.  Its unique style is a key element to our local character but sadly could not be upgraded for modern rail.  From old trucks to a beloved schoolhouse, these paintings harken fond memories.  Part of our world for years, they enriched our lives and are not to be forgotten.  Noted Miller on the impetus for her series, “I want to catch old things before they’re gone – memorializing those things close to our hearts.”

Meet the artist: Miller will host the Gallery on October 26 and November 2, 11, 14 & 15 from 11am to 2:30 pm.

 Also join us for **ART NITE HEALDSBURG**, Thursday, November 5, 5 – 7 pm.  ART NITE Healdsburg, held the 1st Thursday of Every Month, is a community event celebrating art and creativity with over 20 galleries participating.  ArtNiteHealdsburg.com.

title: Shut Up & Write!™ Santa Rosa REMOTE ZOOM FRIDAY
description:
Shut Up & Write!® Wine Country
**This event is hosted on the Shut Up & Write website, so please [sign up here](https://www.shutupwrite.com/series/id2me5JeN600/id2w10OBEA00) for your writing event.**

**ABOUT THE EVENT**
Join us virtually for an hour + of writing using Zoom. Let's keep together as much as we can during these uncertain times and keep on writing. Look for the schedule online and join us.

We’ve discovered that it’s strikingly helpful to write with other writers. See if it’s true for you at 3pm on Friday afternoon. Be it a book, blog, script, essay, dissertation, resume, melody, poem or just plain work stuff, you are invited to write it with us. No one will see what you've written or give you unsolicited advice. Instead of just thinking about writing, come and get some real writing done.

JOIN US!

1. Link available on the Shut Up and Write website..

Please note:

1. If you don't have Zoom set up on your computer yet, leave 15-30 minutes ahead of time to get it set up!
2. If you have difficulty with audio (don't have a microphone set up), as long as you have a speaker, you can call in (you'll see phone numbers when you log in).
3. If you are late, you won't be able to intro with us, but you are still welcome to join in.
4. If you won't be able to make it, please cancel so that the space is available to another writer.

SCHEDULE:
3:00 - quick intros.
around 3:10 - timer starts: write for 70 mins.
4:20 - (the end) wrap up

Wherever you are, we hope to see you online! Keep on writing...
Regards,
Lorraine Segal
source: Meetup: Shut Up & Write Wine Country

title: Napa Primary Care Conference November 4-8, 2026
description:
The Napa Primary Care Conference is a unique educational conference for physicians and medical professionals who care for active and athletic patients or who themselves lead such a lifestyle.

16 HOURS AAFP CME CREDIT

Location

The conference will be held at The Napa Valley Marriott Resort and Spa, conveniently located within minutes of renowned wineries, shopping, attractions, and numerous options for exercise and physical activity.

Course Description

This conference will present very practical information that you can use in your practice. Topics will include common medical and musculoskeletal problems that affect patients who lead an active lifestyle. The focus will be on providing information that will help you diagnose and manage these conditions in the office; so that you can help your patients get moving again and improve their performance. In addition, various topics on healthy lifestyles and personal wellness will make this conference a valuable experience for all attendees.

Intended Audience

The curriculum is directed to Family Medicine, Internal Medicine, Pediatrics, Emergency Medicine, PM and R and Orthopedics specialists as well as Physical Therapists, Athletic Trainers, Physicians Assistants, Nurse Practitioners and others who want to earn Continuing Medical Education from leading physician experts who are outstanding speakers.

Course Learning Objectives

Upon conclusion of this program, participants should be able to:

1. Describe recent advances regarding various medical problems and their impact on the athlete and exercise performance.

2. Identify current recommendations for proper nutrition in active and athletic patients.

3. Illustrate key skills in the diagnosis and management of common musculoskeletal problems encountered by family physicians.

4. Diagnose common problems encountered by patients and effectively treat these conditions.

5. Define common medical-legal issues relevant to the primary care physician.

We hope you can join us for this unique conference in 2024. I look forward to meeting you in Napa!

Sincerely,

Robert Sallis, MD, FACSM, FAAFP

Conference Chairman

Family Medicine Physician

Clinical Professor of Family Medicine

UC Riverside School of Medicine

Kaiser Permanente Medical Center, Fontana, CA

title: Shana Morrison & Caledonia
description:
Doors 6 PM | Show 7 PM

**Shana Morrison’s** musical style has been called pop with a side of blues and a side of rock. She is also known to include other ingredients, like country, R&B and jazz into the mix. Her material seems to be ever-changing and hard to pin down categorically, but what always remains the same is Shana’s unique and wide-ranging voice.

The daughter of legendary Northern Irish musician **Van Morrison**, Shana Morrison began performing with her group Caledonia in the San Francisco Bay area in 1996, releasing their debut CD on her own label, Belfast Violet Records. Since 2002, Shana has toured internationally, including numerous concert dates with her father. She has shared billing with the likes of Bonnie Raitt, John Lee Hooker, and Dr. John, and has played for a variety of festival audiences, including the San Francisco Blues Festival and the Cork Jazz Festival. Her setlist always includes some of Van Morrison’s greatest hits.

**Caledonia** is one of those indefinable bands. Variously described as alt-country and new wave, the group continues to fly its own hybrid tapestry freak flag.

title: Trio Zimbalist
description: The trio is lauded for its masterful interpretations of repertoire spanning from Classical and Romantic masterworks to today's most lauded composers. Since its debut in Athens in 2021, Trio Zimbalist has quickly established itself as one of the world's leading piano trio ensembles. Recent and upcoming performances include the Concertgebouw in Amsterdam, Phillips Collection in Washington, D.C., 92nd Street Y, New York, Toronto Summer Music, Czech Chamber Music Society, St Martin-in-the-Fields in London, Club Monteverdi in Madrid, and Philharmonische Gesellschaft Bremen. The ensemble also has recent and upcoming performances of Beethoven's Triple Concerto with the Greensboro Symphony and the Chamber Orchestra of Philadelphia. The trio's acclaimed recording Piano Trios of Weinberg, Auerbach, and Dvořák was selected as a Gramophone Editor's Choice in March 2024. It was hailed by the magazine as "an astonishingly accomplished debut" and praised by The Stradfor its "wide range of sound, colour and dynamics." Members of the trio-violinist Josef Špaček, cellist Timotheos Gavriilidis-Petrin, and pianist George Xiaoyuan Fu-are in demand across Europe and the U.S. as soloists, chamber musicians, and recitalists. All distinguished alumni of the renowned Curtis Institute of Music, they draw on a lineage of world-class chamber music performance, having studied with teachers representing ensembles including the Guarneri Quartet and the Beaux Arts Trio. Taking its name from famed violin virtuoso Efrem Zimbalist, a towering presence at Curtis as faculty and director for a combined forty years, Trio Zimbalist carries on the violinist's storied legacy through its commitment to artistic excellence. Trio Zimbalist is represented by Curtis Artist Management at Curtis Institute of Music.

title: Sweeney Todd
description:
Sweeney Todd is largely considered one of Stephen Sondheim’s masterpieces. With it, he aimed to create a musical that could “scare the hell out of everyone,” and yet, somehow, be funny.

The story centers around Sweeney Todd, an unjustly exiled barber who returns to London, seeking vengeance against the lecherous judge who framed him and ravaged his young wife. The road to revenge leads Todd to Mrs. Lovett, a resourceful proprietress of a failing pie shop, above which, he opens a new barber practice. Mrs. Lovett’s luck sharply shifts when Todd’s thirst for blood inspires the integration of an ingredient into her meat pies that has the people of 19th Century London lining up…and the carnage has only just begun!

\***Content Advisory:** Adult language and violent themes, as well as controversial pie recipes. Recommended for 12+.

title: The Book of Will, a dramatic comedy presented by Solano College Theatre
description:
Solano College Theatre presents

The Book of Will

📆November 6-22, 2026

📌4000 Suisun Valley Road, Fairfield CA

🎟 Tickets: www.solanocollegetheatre.org

📞 \(707\) 864-7100

Where there’s a will, there’s a way.

“The Book of Will” brings to life the chaotic, hilarious, passionate, and mostly true endeavor to compile Shakespeare’s plays into the legendary First Folio!

About the show: Without William Shakespeare, we wouldn’t have literary masterpieces like “Romeo and Juliet.” But without Henry Condell and John Heminges, we would have lost half of Shakespeare’s plays forever! After the death of their friend and mentor, the two actors are determined to compile the First Folio and preserve the words that shaped their lives. They’ll just have to borrow, beg, and band together to get it done. Amidst the noise and color of Elizabethan London, The Book of Will finds an unforgettable true story of love, loss, and laughter, and sheds new light on a man you may think you know.

location: Occidental Center for the Arts, 3850 Doris Murphy Court, Occidental, CA 95465
description:
Occidental Center for the Arts presents Electric Tumbleweed! One of Sonoma County's finest bands returns for our listening and dancing pleasure.
Tickets are $20/$15 for OCA members. Doors open at 7:30 PM. No dogs. Refreshments available. Free parking.
Get Tickets
Electric Tumbleweed is a psychedelic outlaw country group based in Sonoma County, California. Founded in 2019 by members rooted in bluegrass, country, and psychedelic rock, the music is a hard driving mixture of twangy guitar and psychedelic noise, held together by a steady rhythm section with the cry of pedal steel layered in between it all. Electric Tumbleweed has maintained steady momentum in the Northern California music scene; backing David Nelson (New Riders of the Purple Sage) on multiple occasions; most notably at the Mystic Theater with guest Mark Karan (Ratdog) for a sold out performance. Electric Tumbleweed performed regularly at Phil Lesh’s Terrapin Crossroads as a solo group as well as with Scott Law, Barry Sless (Phil Lesh and Friends) and Dave Zirbel (Sammy Hagar Band) are regular pedal steel players in the group. The band has been invited to play multiple festivals and events including The String Cheese Incident’s Hog Farm Hideaway, Ain’t Necessarily Dead Fest (backing David Nelson). We aim to keep our goals high, and to perform high quality music; focusing on writing and arranging new songs, and booking future tour dates. We are excited to release our debut full-length album in October 2021, which features Sam Bush (New Grass Revival), Barry Sless (Phil Lesh & Friends), and Lester and Dylan Chambers (The Chambers Brothers). The album features the artwork of Stanley Mouse/Jennae Bennett and was engineered and mastered by Grammy winning Oz Fritz (Tom Waits).

title: Grant-Lee Phillips & Grant Lee Buffalo & Damon Wyckoff
description:
“I’m drawing on the urgency of the moment,” reflects Grant-Lee Phillips. “The things that eat away in the late hours…”

That urgency inspired the headlong rush of his new album Widdershins – in which Grant-Lee Phillips invests the insight, nuance, and wit that has distinguished his songcraft over the past three decades. 

Exploring folk, alternative, pop and Americana, Phillips’ band Grant Lee Buffalo was a seminal ‘90s mainstay. Even in the wake of disbanding in ’99, albums like Fuzzy and Mighty Joe Moon remain enigmatic treasures, that new generations are drawn to. So much so, that Grant Lee Buffalo embarked on a string of reunion dates in 2011. The group signed a deal with Chrysalis/Blue Rain Coat in 2018 and a major reissue of the catalogue is currently underway.

As for Phillips, his career has constantly evolved, diving into deeper adventurous waters with each project. Being a songwriter and a multi-instrumentalist, he’s embraced the freedom of being his own producer. “For me, production is about honoring and delivering the song, baring witness to the spirit in the room. It is so much about communication, finding that common language among musicians and technicians - which is often wordless, by the way.” Fans have come to accept that Phillips would always prioritize creative discovery, while resisting the expected. 

Something he could never expect occurred in 2001 when Phillips was approached about a role on a newly burgeoning TV show called The Gilmore Girls. “The Town Troubadour was sort of a cartoon version of myself. I had no idea it was going to snowball into multiple seasons, coffee mugs and syndication as it did. The show turned a lot of new people onto my music.”

Acting wouldn’t curb Phillips’ consistent output however. Mobilize, Virginia Creeper, Nineteeneighties, Strangelet and Little Moon would follow – each a document of his life in that moment.

On his 2012 release Walking in the Green Corn he drew from his Native American heritage. A year later Phillips relocated from Los Angeles to Nashville, marking a new creative chapter, inspiring The Narrows. The release of Widdershins in 2018 brings the current count to nine solo albums and four with Grant Lee Buffalo.

His eyes remain fixed on the work at hand and that of tomorrow. His tour schedule finds him circling the globe many times over in a given year. Constant movement, physically and creatively is almost a mantra. Say’s Phillips, “I could never sit still.“

Returning to the First Mark November 7th, 2026 - 11:00am-3:00pm Attendance Price: $130.00 Ages 16+In this new workshop we will explore drawing and abstract mark making through play, curiosity, and child-like wonder.Before we learned to write words, we communicated through marks. As children, we drew with curiosity, freedom, and a sense of play - without worrying about getting it "right” and without fear of getting our hands dirty.  We played in the dirt and we made things.  This workshop invites you to reconnect with that creative spirit through abstract mark making and intuitive drawing.Using a variety of drawing tools and materials, we'll explore line, texture, rhythm, and gesture as a personal visual language. Through guided exercises and playful experimentation, you'll discover how letting go of expectations can open the door to greater creativity and self-expression.Whether you're an experienced artist or simply curious about abstract drawing, you'll leave with new techniques, greater confidence, and a renewed sense of creative freedom. No drawing experience is necessary - just a willingness to explore. Returning to the first mark means:→ reconnecting with curiosity→ slowing down and truly seeing→ discovering the language within ordinary things→ responding intuitively→ building something personal through lines and marksParticipant must bring the following:Note: There is no need to buy expensive materials, please consider what you already have.  If you’re missing something, let the instructor know, Sebastopol Center for the Arts has a minimal amount of these supplies available to borrow.Apron or clothing you don't mind getting paint onBlack gesso or black acrylic paintSpray bottle with water Acrylic paint: two or three earthy colors such as burnt umber, raw sienna, or yellow ochre.  If you don’t have these specific colors, no need to purchase them, just bring whatever you haveA small container, like a glass jar, to pour the gesso inA variety of paint brushes (3 to 5) from very thin to thickA container for waterDifferent types of paper to draw on, from small to large sheets.  Examples: recycled book pages, copy paper, drawing pad, newsprint, brown paper bags, vintage papers with or without illustrations but nothing too dark or too busy. Two black pens or markers with different tipsGlue stickScissorsPaper towelsThe class will begin with a talk and a demonstration, so please plan to arrive early to allow time to settle in.A short lunch break will be held from 12:30 to 1:00 PM. title: Antarctica: The Frozen Desert | Photographs by Vegar Abelsnes
description:
1st Street Gallery at WTRSHD will present “Antarctica: The Frozen Desert,” a new body of fine art photography by Vegar Abelsnes, opening September 26th, 2026, and on view September through November.  The exhibition marks a deliberate turn in Abelsnes’ photography; after more than two decades of working in a commercial and advertising capacity, he has embarked on a career as a photo and field guide in the polar regions. The exhibit features work generated over 6 voyages to the Antarctic Peninsula. He is returning to Antarctica in January and will add the Falklands and South Georgia to his list of destinations to guide and photograph.

Traveling to some of the most remote and inhospitable coastlines on Earth, Abelsnes has photographed a landscape that exists almost entirely outside of human time. The ice in these images began forming millions of years ago, while Homo sapiens have only existed for roughly 300,000 years. Defined by such a scale, Antarctica is less a place than a record — vast, indifferent, treacherous, and staggeringly beautiful, holding a kind of cosmic truth that Abelsnes says is more important now than ever before.

title: Holistic Horse Training in Heart and Mind Equine
description:
Bring your horse or learn with the Heart & Mind Equine herd in this hands-on exploration of communication, connection, and kind leadership.

Offered by Heart & Mind Equine Rescue. Meet our rescued therapy horses, explore our volunteer program, and learn about holistic horse keeping and equine-assisted services \(e.g., therapy, coaching, leadership, and team building with horses\). No experience is necessary. All are welcome, including both horse and mental health professionals.

A Different Approach to Horse Training

What happens when we stop thinking about horse training simply as getting a horse to do what we want and start learning to communicate in a language horses naturally understand?

Join us for a 90-minute experiential introduction to Holistic Horse Training with lifelong horsewoman and equine-assisted learning facilitator Alane Freund.

Horses naturally communicate through movement, energy, boundaries, responsiveness, and connection. Their herd relationships include both leadership and following, with every member playing an important role.

Alane describes these dynamics as ranking and linking: leadership in service of relationship, paired with the connection that makes relationship possible.

Holistic Horse Training uses this deeper understanding of herd dynamics to help us communicate with horses through leadership that is clear, kind, respectful, and connected.

What You’ll Learn

Alane will draw from natural horsemanship, TTouch, equine behavior and herd dynamics, and her own Holistic Horse Training exercises to explore:

Reading equine communication and body language

Clear, kind boundaries

Leadership without force

Building trust and connection

Practical training tools and techniques

What horses can teach us about effective leadership in our own lives

Bring Your Horse or Learn With the Herd

Have a horse you’d like to work with? Bring them along.

No horse? No problem. You can participate with members of the Heart & Mind Equine herd.

Come ready to learn, experiment, ask questions, and discover a more connected way of working with horses.

Heart and Mind Equine | Woodacre, CA | Saturday, November 7 • Starts at 9 AM

title: Park Rx—Intermediate Hiking for Fitness Fall 2026
description:
The program leaders will guide you on 8 weekly hikes with the challenge increasing each week. Leaders will have group discussions about gear, hydration, hiking poles, first aid and pacing, etc. The group's final hike aims for Bald Mountain, where hikers can enjoy stunning vistas.

The following is a list of possible routes specifically selected for this hiking series:

description:
**Is Food a Problem for You? You Are Not Alone.**

Overeaters Anonymous (OA) is a fellowship of people who support each other in recovering from compulsive eating and food behaviors. If you feel you have a problem with food, OA welcomes you—no matter what your background, beliefs, or eating habits. 

We hold an in-person newcomer meeting on first, second and fourth **Saturdays of the month from 9:45 - 10:15 AM at** ​**Unitarian Universalist Congregation of Marin, 240 Channing Way, San Rafael CA 94903**. Contact: Sue M. 415-298-6792​. You may view all North Bay OA in-person and online meetings at https://www.northbayoa.org/meetings.html

In OA, members experience **spiritual, emotional, and physical recovery** by practicing the **Twelve Steps** and living by their spiritual principles—one day at a time.

OA is **not** a diet club or calorie-counting program.

Members have different plans of eating.

OA does **not** endorse any specific food plan. 

If food is causing problems in your life, you don’t have to struggle alone. Recovery is possible, and help is available.

**Visit:** https://www.northbayoa.org/

**Find a meeting:** https://www.northbayoa.org/meetings.html

EAMES & EAMES: Meet the couple who Defined Modern Design

Created in collaboration with the Eames Institute of Infinite Curiosity.

EAMES & EAMES explores the iterative, hands-on, and human-centered approach of Charles & Ray Eames. Through furniture, toys, paintings, graphics, and personal belongings collected over their lifetimes, this groundbreaking exhibition looks beyond the iconic Eames chairs to reveal the breadth of their creative practice. More than any single object, their work opened doors to new and unexpected ways of seeing, thinking, making, and understanding the world—ideas that continue to inspire us today.

title: Intro to California Coastal Range Geology
description: Join us and explore Galbreath Preserve. title: Marin Arts & Crafts Show
description:
Marin Arts & Crafts Show returns to the Marin Center Exhibit Hall November 6–8, filling the hall with more than 200 exhibits of fine craft, art and artisan goods. Arriving just as the holiday season gets underway, the three-day market brings together an exciting mix of artists, artisans and craftspeople for a weekend of art, handcraft and seasonal discoveries.

Inspired by the Arts & Crafts movement, the show celebrates craftsmanship, thoughtful design and artistic expression in its many forms. Visitors will find jewelry, ceramics, textiles, glass, woodwork, fine art, furniture, wearable art and specialty foods from artisan food makers. From hand-dyed silks and sculptural ceramics to finely crafted jewelry and heirloom-quality woodworking, the market brings together traditional techniques, fresh ideas and contemporary design.

Throughout the weekend, visitors can talk with artists about their work, watch demonstrations and explore the many forms of handcraft represented at the show. It's a chance to see the details up close, hear how things are made and get to know some of the people behind the work.

The November show brings a festive atmosphere to the Marin Center, with a bustling marketplace of fine crafts, art and artisan foods. Visitors can enjoy wine tasting, sample seasonal treats from specialty food merchants and listen to live music throughout the weekend. Free opportunity drawings offer chances to win wonderful prizes donated by participating artisans, adding to the excitement.

With free admission and free parking, Marin Arts & Crafts Show is an inviting way to spend a fall afternoon with family and friends. As the holidays approach, the market is also a wonderful place to discover distinctive gifts while supporting independent artisans.

**Marin Arts & Crafts Show** November 6–8, 2026 Friday–Sunday, 10 a.m.–5 p.m. Marin Center Exhibit Hall 20 Avenue of the Flags, San Rafael, CA **Free admission & free parking**

title: Rituals of Care: Buddhist Chant and Culture
description:
Learn to chant with Chenxing Han and Trent Walker

What is the role of chant in Buddhist practice? How does it shape communities of belonging and cultures of care?

During this daylong, we will engage in a variety of chanting practices from across the Buddhist world, with a special emphasis on the Theravāda tradition as transmitted in mainland Southeast Asia. We’ll explore the musical and textual dimensions of chant, as well as its ritual possibilities. Our charge as a group will be to embody chant as an expression of care for ourselves, our loved ones, and the world.

There will be time to reflect on questions of voice, language, and lineage. Nearly every Buddhist throughout history has engaged in recitation and other practices of aspiration, concentration, and devotion. Our day together invites us into kinship with them as we, too, experience the healing resonances of these practices.

All are warmly welcome to participate; no previous chanting experience is required.

description: Join us for a 3-hour hands-on sourdough making class at Gold Ridge Organic Farms, led by Monica Flaherty of the Sebastopol Sourdough Company. Spend three immersive hours in our charming Apple Cottage learning the art and science of sourdough bread making. Monica will walk you through everything you need to know — how wild yeast and fermentation work, why sourdough differs from commercial yeast bread, and how to read your dough. You'll also cover starter care and feeding, mixing and hydration ratios, shaping and scoring techniques, and the secrets to achieving that perfect crust and open crumb. Every guest will leave with an active starter, a feeding schedule and care guide, a shaped dough in a banneton ready to bake at home, and their very own apron to take home as a keepsake. The experience also includes a ride across the farm on our beloved apple-themed trolley to the Apple Cottage.

title: You are Invited to North Bay Speech Masters Toastmasters Club Meeting
description:
Whether it's improving our health, focusing on professional advancement, learning a new skill, it is often helpful to obtain someone to help learn new skills like speaking without preparation. The group at Toastmasters can help.

We call speaking without preparation, impromptu speaking. If you want to learn new Impromptu speaking skills, Toastmasters can help. During the meeting, we will practice our impromptu speaking skills during our session we call Table Topics. During the Table Topics, the speaker is given a question, and they are asked to speak for 60 seconds to 2 minutes about the question.

Outside Toastmasters, impromptu speaking happens constantly. You might recognize it in moments such as:

--Being asked for your opinion in a meeting

--Responding to a follow-up question during a presentation

--Introducing yourself or someone else unexpectedly

--Handling a difficult or unplanned question

You can learn tips and tricks about speaking off the cuff at our meeting. Won't you join us and learn

what Toastmasters can do to help you on your professional journey.

Feel free to contact us for the zoon link at our website under the "Contact Us" button. The website is https://3038.toastmastersclubs.org

We hold meetings online and in-person. If joining us in-person, there is limited parking in the front lot. Once in the front door, please sign in at the computer to obtain a visitors' badge. \(IUsually, there is a sheet by the computer telling you how to log in for Toastmasters.\) If the sheet isn't there, the clerk at the desk can help. Then take the elevator down to the second floor, and take a left out of the elevator and a left at the hall and come down to the meeting room.

title: Senderos: Los Wappo en Wilikos
description:
\[Translated to English below\] Aprende acerca de las historias y tradiciones de la tribu Wappo, una de las tribus originarias de esta área, en esta caminata familiar de 2 millas. Nos reuniremos en el estacionamiento del granero blanco (el White Barn) y caminaremos el sendero Meadow mientras escuchamos acerca de la historia cultural de los Wappo en una de sus aldeas ancestral, Wilikos, hoy en día parte de Sugarloaf. 

Evento gratuito; requiere registración. Hay transportación disponible gratuita dentro de un radio de 20 millas al parque para familias que la necesiten. Para detalles y registración, visita EVENT LINK

Alternativamente, llama a Mario (707-387-4087), Alma (707-247-5767), entre martes y sábado) o escríbenos a senderos@sonomaecologycenter.org. ¿No puedes acompañarnos ese día? ¡Guarda la fecha el 5 de diciembre para más aventuras!

Senderos Naturales es parcialmente respaldado por una beca de Parks California.

Fotografía cortesía de Alma Shaw

\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_\_

Learn about the history and traditions of the Mishewal Wappo Tribe, one of the original groups to live in this area. On this family hike, will walk approximately 2 miles along the Meadow trail while we listen to the cultural history of the Wappo peoples in one of their ancestral villages called Wilikios, today found in Sugarloaf.

This event is planned around a primarily Latino audience and will be conducted in Spanish. Families from underrepresented groups are welcome to join.
