title: An Evening with Zoë Lewis
description:
Affectionately know as “a band in a body,” Zoë Lewis plays vintage jazz and world beat grooves on anything from the piano to ukulele to the spoons! 

Originally from the UK, this astonishing singer-songwriter has called Provincetown her home for the last 32 years. She's traveled to over 70 countries picking up musical grooves and stories along the way, released ten albums of original material, toured with the Indigo Girls, Judy Collins, Richie Havens, Nanci Griffiths and has even opened for Pat Benatar on the ukulele! 

Her songs have won numerous accolades, have appeared in films, on Broadway, in commercials, and most recently on the Netflix kid show *StoryBots*. She’s written 3 musicals that received rave reviews, performs for OLIVIA cruises, and takes her show to Puerto Vallarta, Mexico every winter.

Zoe will be joined by the fabulous KATE WOLF on bass.

An evening with Zoe Lewis will leave you with long-lasting joy. Join us!

description: Callie Watts is a singer/songwriter from Northern California who was raised on classical music, The Beatles and The Beach Boys before discovering Joni Mitchell, Elton John, Stevie Wonder, Paul Simon, Billy Joel, Carole King, and all the great writers of the ’60s and 70’s who have influenced her sound and writing style. After graduating high school, Callie began playing and performing solo, as well as in local and bay area bands of different genres. She’s played blues with Eric Lindell and the Reds, funky soul with Phatty, and jazz/swing with Savoy Swingers along with many other various projects. Callie has taken turns throughout her career as a keyboardist, guitarist, writer, and lead/backing vocalist, and she’s currently a member of the dynamic Sonoma County funk rock band Burrows and Dilbeck, having joined in 2010 as part of the former band Frobeck. Over time, she’s had the honor of opening for acts such as Bootsy Collins, Elvin Bishop, Huey Lewis and The News, War, Ozomatli, Bill Champlin, Booker T, and the B52s. Callie continues to perform frequently as an acoustic solo artist, focusing on developing a core audience and a buzz for her original material. description:
Gradina is a Balkan music ensemble based in California’s North Bay area.
We celebrate the seasons and their festivals through song and dance, bringing Old World rituals to new light and new generations to revel in the staying power of gratitude for life on Earth.
We sing both a cappella and with instrumental accompaniment. We lean toward traditional songs and arrangements. We present “sit-down” concerts for choral listening as well as dance concerts, and we are also available to teach most of the dances we present. We are honored to play with many Balkan musicians from near and far, and every concert is different, often with a different array of performers alongside the core group.
Our special guests will be Gaelen Genetti on Bulgarian kaval and Christina Penrose on clarinet.
Tickets are $25/$15 for OCA members. Doors open at 6:30 PM.

title: Trio da Paz
description: Grammy-nominated Trio da Paz, one of the most visible Brazilian jazz groups in the world featuring three of Brazil's most-in-demand musicians: Romero Lubambo on guitar, Nilson Matta on bass and Duduka da Fonseca on drums and percussion. They formed in 1986 and will be celebrating their 40th anniversary at THE 222 in an exclusive West Coast appearance. Together, Trio da Paz performs with a strong sense of cohesion, bringing energy, imagination, and a deep musical connection to their work. The result is a trio that continues to create distinctive, personal music, blending Brazilian traditions with elements of modern jazz. Trio da Paz's sound reflects a thoughtful integration of Brazilian musical styles and jazz improvisation, drawing on the harmonies of bossa nova, the rhythms of samba, and the melodic intricacy of choro. Their acoustic trio format-guitar, bass, and drums-allows for close interaction among the musicians, fostering a conversational approach that highlights both rhythmic interplay and harmonic nuance. While grounded in tradition, the group approaches familiar forms with flexibility, allowing the music to evolve in unexpected but natural directions. Each member, established on the New York jazz scene as both a leader and collaborator, contributes to a collective identity shaped by original compositions alongside interpretations of Brazilian repertoire.

Genre bending originals add elements of jazz, blues, vintage pop and folk, while dazzling new arrangements bring old classics and deep cuts to life.

Where there’s a will, there’s a way.

“The Book of Will” brings to life the chaotic, hilarious, passionate, and mostly true endeavor to compile Shakespeare’s plays into the legendary First Folio!

About the show: Without William Shakespeare, we wouldn’t have literary masterpieces like “Romeo and Juliet.” But without Henry Condell and John Heminges, we would have lost half of Shakespeare’s plays forever! After the death of their friend and mentor, the two actors are determined to compile the First Folio and preserve the words that shaped their lives. They’ll just have to borrow, beg, and band together to get it done. Amidst the noise and color of Elizabethan London, The Book of Will finds an unforgettable true story of love, loss, and laughter, and sheds new light on a man you may think you know.

title: Maynard Lyndon Artist Exhibition
description:
Exhibition: 10.01 through 11.15 Reception: Thursday, 10.01 from 4pm-6pm The Sea Ranch Lodge

Playful Ways of Seeing Now 85, Maynard has been ‘drawing+painting’ and ‘inventing+model-making’ since early childhood — always encouraged to ‘look+learn+create+share.’ He’s been doing so for decades; his ‘sharing’ has been in the realms of teaching and in developing products for the housewares and furniture industries, and designing retail environments, including galleries and design shops, beginning in 1967 when he opened ColorForm — a small toy shop in Santa Monica, specializing in hand-made playthings.

As an artist and designer, color + form reign importantly in Maynard’s mind — in his ‘seeing+sharing’ through creating objects and images, sometimes ‘playfully.’ The artworks in this exhibit — whether his 3D ‘Looking Boxes’ or his paintings+drawings — are ones he’s made in 2026.

We hold an in-person meetings at 9:30 on Sunday mornings at Church of the Nazarene, 18980 Arnold Drive, Sonoma, CA \(a small room directly off of parking lot; look for the sign posted\) and newcomers are always welcome.

You may view all North Bay OA in-person and online meetings at https://www.northbayoa.org/meetings.html

OA is not a diet club or calorie-counting program.

Members have different plans of eating.

OA does not endorse any specific food plan. 

Visit: https://www.northbayoa.org/

title: Artazan Handcraft Market
description:
Artazan Handcraft Market returns to Pasadena November 14–15, bringing together artists, artisans, craftspeople and the community for a weekend celebrating creativity and work made by hand.

Inspired by the ideas behind the Arts & Crafts movement, the handcraft market celebrates creativity, thoughtful design, skilled work and the people behind the things we bring into our lives. That spirit is reflected in a contemporary and wide-ranging mix of handcraft, encompassing many different materials, traditions and creative approaches.

Held at the Pasadena Convention Center, the two-day market will be filled with work from independent artists and artisans across an eclectic mix of mediums. Visitors might discover jewelry and metalsmithing, ceramics and glass, crochet and fiber art, woodworking and handcrafted clocks, painting and mixed media, wearable art, leatherwork, home décor, artisan foods and much more. From time-honored skills to unexpected new ideas, the market reflects the remarkable variety of what people are creating by hand today.

The weekend will also connect with Pasadena’s broader creative community, bringing together local and regional artists, arts organizations, educators and visitors. Guests can talk directly with artists, learn about their materials and techniques, take part in hands-on workshops, watch demonstrations and enjoy live music throughout the weekend.

Taking place at the beginning of the holiday season, the November market offers an alternative to mass-produced holiday shopping, with distinctive gifts, original art, artisan foods and objects for the home, while directly supporting independent artists and small creative businesses.

More than a place to shop, Artazan offers an opportunity to see handcraft up close, discover something unexpected and experience the incredible range of things being made by hand today.

EVENT DETAILS Artazan Handcraft Market November 14–15, 2026 Pasadena Convention Center • Pasadena, California Saturday & Sunday • 10 a.m.–5 p.m.

Tickets, workshops, exhibitor information and additional details are available at Artazan.com.

title: EAMES & EAMES: Meet the couple who Defined Modern Design
location: The MAC - Napa Valley Museum of Art & Culture
description:
EAMES & EAMES: Meet the couple who Defined Modern Design

Created in collaboration with the Eames Institute of Infinite Curiosity.

EAMES & EAMES explores the iterative, hands-on, and human-centered approach of Charles & Ray Eames. Through furniture, toys, paintings, graphics, and personal belongings collected over their lifetimes, this groundbreaking exhibition looks beyond the iconic Eames chairs to reveal the breadth of their creative practice. More than any single object, their work opened doors to new and unexpected ways of seeing, thinking, making, and understanding the world—ideas that continue to inspire us today.

Curated by Llisa Demetrios, Co-Founder & The Lucia Eames Chief Curator of the Eames Institute of Infinite Curiosity.

title: Veterans Holiday Market
description:
The Sonoma VFW Auxiliary Post 1943 will host its 4th Annual Veterans Holiday Market on Saturday, November 14, from 10 a.m. to 4 p.m., and Sunday, November 15, from 10 a.m. to 3 p.m. at the Veterans Memorial Building, 126 First St. West, Sonoma.

The two-day holiday market will feature one-of-a-kind, limited-edition goods handcrafted by local artists and makers. With several vendors participating, shoppers will have an opportunity to find unique gifts while supporting the Auxiliary’s mission of helping those who have served and their loved ones.

The Native Daughters of the Golden West, Sonoma Parlor No. 209, will also host a special community activity, “Make a Veteran a Christmas Card.” Community members of all ages are invited to create handmade holiday cards that will be delivered to area veterans living in assisted living facilities and nursing homes.

The Veterans Holiday Market is free and open to the public, with a special invitation extended to military members, veterans and their families. Proceeds from the event will help provide assistance to veterans and military families who are experiencing hardship.

The VFW Auxiliary is an all-volunteer service organization whose members include the spouses, parents, grandparents, brothers, sisters and other family members of those who have served in overseas combat. Since 1934, members of Sonoma VFW Auxiliary Post 1943 have worked to support those who have served and strengthen the community around them.

The Auxiliary’s community service efforts have included toy and monetary donations to Toys for Tots, Christmas gifts and cards for veterans at the Yountville Veterans Home, as well as clothing and food drives benefiting local emergency service organizations.

The Veterans Holiday Market is an opportunity for the entire community to come together during the holiday season—not only to shop and celebrate, but also to show appreciation for those who have served and to remind veterans and their loved ones that they are valued, remembered and not alone.

title: A Taste of Italy at Centennial Mountain Tasting Room
description:
For wine drinkers eager to experience world-class wines made in California from Italian varieties, the Centennial Mountain Tasting Room is a must during any trip to Sonoma County. Located just off the plaza in the charming town of Healdsburg near famed restaurants, boutiques and galleries, the Centennial Mountain Tasting Room is a destination that invites discovery. Founded by the acclaimed team that guides renowned Pinot Noir and Chardonnay producer Rhys Vineyards, Centennial Mountain was established to explore Italian grape varieties grown on its acclaimed Centennial Mountain Vineyard in the rugged mountains of Northern Sonoma County.

The Centennial Mountain Vineyard Tasting features the winery’s coveted Nebbiolo, and the pioneering Carricante and Nerello Mascalese wines, among others. To showcase how beautifully the wines pair with food, the winery also offers a delicious Wine and Sushi Pairing from nearby Asahi Sushi, one of Healdsburg’s most popular dining destinations.

Guests can also enhance their tasting experience with a curated salumi board from Journeyman Meat Company. This generous accompaniment features six house-made salumi, crostini, cornichons, olives, and a selection of local cheese that serves 2 to 5 guests.

title: Art Exhibit: Aspirations
description:
Date: FOR IMMEDIATE RELEASE  9/15/26

**OCTOBER EXHIBIT: ASPIRATIONS**

EXHIBIT DATES **– September 28 – October 25, 2026**

**RECEPTION: SATURDAY, October 3, 2026, 3-6 pm: Join us to meet Laura Roney and Linda Loveland Reid and learn about their art and inspiration.  Be sure to take part in the Gallery’s free monthlong drawing for a beautiful work by a Gallery artist.  Refreshments will be served.**

Sonoma County artist, **Laura Roney,** unveils **Aspirations**, a new collection of paintings in oil, celebrating the unique differing goals people set during our lives, challenging us to take bold steps forward.  Of universal inspiration**, Aspiration and Awe** splashes the Milky Way’s starry brilliance across the heavens, capturing our imagination and hope as worldly cares are left behind.  Moving from natural forces to human endeavor, looking toward social change, **Aspiring to Vote**, the portrait of a hopeful suffragette, evokes the dream for a better future.  A lifetime goal for many, the marathon, **Aspiring for 26.2,** captures the early morning excitement waiting for start times.  “People doing ordinary things but dreaming larger for the future has been a great inspiration for this series.  I hope folks will be inspired by the boldness of people’s dreams,” commented Roney on her inspiration for the work.

Art has been a lifelong passion for Roney.  Beginning her art studies at a young age, whatever avenue she was pursuing in life, she continued her artistic endeavors.  After a successful career in microbiology and pharmaceutical research, a family move to Northern California enabled Roney to focus on her art.  She received her MFA from Academy of Art University, San Francisco.

Meet the artist: Roney will host the Gallery on September 30 and October 1 from 11am to 6 pm.

The Stairway Smallworks Showcase features Linda Loveland Reid’s **Intentional Chaos,** a collection of exciting mixed-media works that explode with excitement and energy. Random patterns, amorphous shapes and dancing dribbles magically coalesce into bold statements.  Intriguing and compelling, like interlocking gears, in **Patterns of Memory** multiple patterns interlock on fields of gold and black.  “I love throwing ink, paint and even coffee onto a blank canvas and creating through instinct, gesture and emotion.  Distilling energy into smaller works brings new challenges and some happy surprises,” noted Reid on her creative process.

Meet the artist: Reid will host the Gallery on October 23 from 11am to 6 pm.

 Also join us for **ART NITE HEALDSBURG**, Thursday, October 1, 5 – 7 pm.  ART NITE Healdsburg, held the 1st Thursday of Every Month, is a community event celebrating art and creativity with over 20 galleries participating.  ArtNiteHealdsburg.com.

Upstairs Art Gallery, 306 Center Street, Healdsburg, CA 95448. (707) 431-4214.: OPEN DAILY: 11am – 6 pm.    **www.upstairsart gallery.net** 

For further information: Contact: Beverly Bird, Press Contact, at bvdrio@sonic.net or 707-799-1490.

title: Art Exhibit: Endless Inspiration
description:
Date: FOR IMMEDIATE RELEASE  10/12/26

**NOVEMBER EXHIBIT: ENDLESS INSPIRATION**

EXHIBIT DATES **– October 26  – November 22, 2026**

**RECEPTION: SATURDAY, November 7, 2026, 3-6 pm: Join us to meet Ron Sumner and Karen Miller and learn about their art and inspiration.  Be sure to take part in the Gallery’s free monthlong drawing for a beautiful work by a Gallery artist.  Refreshments will be served.**

Sonoma County artist, **Ron Sumner,** presents **Endless Inspiration**, a collection of new paintings and classic works that highlight his lifelong love of nature featuring landscapes, animals and wildlife, with a special focus on birds.  The essence of this golden state shines forth in “California Hills,” a large oil painting of a sweep of oak covered hills.   Turning to wildlife, Sumner’s masterful watercolor rendition in the “Young Fox” captures its wild nature on stark alert.  And the compelling presence of a most majestic bird is beautifully memorialized in his “Blue Heron” watercolor.  Other birds depicted in his works include parrots, penguins and owls.  “In my painting, I always strive to translate my emotional response to the world of nature around us – to share this deep feeling with those who view my work,” commented Sumner on his inspiration.

A lifelong Northern Californian, Sumner began his art training in school.  After earning a BFA from the California College of Arts & Crafts, he was a technical illustrator for a number of years before transitioning to a full-time fine arts painter.  With an emphasis in watercolor, he has won numerous awards, including Best of Show at the Society of Western Artists.  His portrait of John F. Kennedy is part of the permanent collection at the John F. Kennedy Library.  He has exhibited widely and was part of the Veterans Art Show for CA vets in 2023.

Meet the artist: Sumner will co-host Art Nite on 11/5 from 5 pm to 7 pm.

The Stairway Smallworks Showcase features **Karen Miller’**s **Historic Gems,** featuring pastel paintings that honor our history – local artifacts that are disappearing.  Highlighting this exhibit, “Ghost Bridge,” an early 20th century railroad bridge known as Healdsburg Railroad Bridge is soon to give way for the Smart Train.  Its unique style is a key element to our local character but sadly could not be upgraded for modern rail.  From old trucks to a beloved schoolhouse, these paintings harken fond memories.  Part of our world for years, they enriched our lives and are not to be forgotten.  Noted Miller on the impetus for her series, “I want to catch old things before they’re gone – memorializing those things close to our hearts.”

Meet the artist: Miller will host the Gallery on October 26 and November 2, 11, 14 & 15 from 11am to 2:30 pm.

 Also join us for **ART NITE HEALDSBURG**, Thursday, November 5, 5 – 7 pm.  ART NITE Healdsburg, held the 1st Thursday of Every Month, is a community event celebrating art and creativity with over 20 galleries participating.  ArtNiteHealdsburg.com.

description:
Welcome poets, writers, and artists of Vallejo. My name is Ray, and I am your host of I NEED A MIC OPEN MIC.

Whether you carry poems in your chest, songs in your spirit, or stories that have been waiting for the right moment — this is your invitation.

We gather not just to perform, but to connect. To celebrate the raw, the real, and the unapologetically human art of expression. Every voice matters here. Every perspective adds to the pulse of this room.

But understand — this is a space built on respect. While we welcome passion, depth, and honesty, we do not tolerate hate, disrespect, or harmful rhetoric. Heavy political agendas that divide rather than inspire have no place here. 

This stage is for expression, not oppression.

Bring your truth. Bring your courage. Bring your art.

Come share. Come listen. Come feel something.

Because someone in that room might need exactly what you have to say.

I NEED A MIC — and maybe, so do you.

About the Poets
Marjorie Stein
is the author of
unRavel,
which was selected by Elaine Equi for the 2025 Marsh Hawk Press Poetry Prize
An Atlas of Lost Causes,
Marjorie’s first book, was published by Kelsey Street Press in 2011. Another poetry project,
In the Hinges of the World
, was shortlisted for the Lost Horse Press 2020 Idaho Prize for Poetry. Her work has appeared, or is forthcoming in
American Poetry Journal, Blood Orange Review, The Denver Quarterly, Interim, Marsh Hawk Press Chapter One Series, Mary, New American Writing, VOLT,
and other publications. Marjorie lives in Northern California, with her wife, where she is privileged to spend time playing with words.
www.marjoriestein.org
Kathleen Winter
is the author of
Transformer, I will not kick my friends,
and
Nostalgia for the Criminal Past.
Her collection
Serial Fabulist
is forthcoming from Texas Review Press in early 2027. Her poems have appeared in
The New Republic, The New Statesman, Cincinnati Review, Agni, Yale Review, Gulf Coast, Tupelo Quarterly,
and
Michigan Quarterly Review.
Her work has been supported by fellowships from the Texas Institute of Letters, the University of Texas at Austin, Heinrich Böll Cottage, Maison Dora Maar, Cill Rialaig Project, James Merrill House, and the Sewanee Writers’ Conference. Awards include the Poetry Society of America The Writer Magazine/Emily Dickinson Award and the Rochelle Ratner Memorial Prize. Kathleen lives in Glen Ellen, California.
Claire Drucker
is the current Sonoma County Poet Laureate. She is a Jewish lesbian mom, educational consultant, poet, and dancer. Her first book-length collection of poems,
The Life You Gave Me

CA Quarterly, Jewish Literary Journal, Rust & Moth, Epiphany, Puerto del Sol

Women Artists Datebook.

rendezvous

is this the body / if hovers

title: Richard Heinberg: A Celebration of His Life and Legacy
description:
***Author • Musician • Senior Fellow at Post Carbon Institute • Environmental Educator • Artist • Husband • Friend***

You are warmly invited to join family, friends, colleagues, and admirers from around the world on **November 15th** as we come together to celebrate the extraordinary life and legacy of **Richard Heinberg**.

A Senior Fellow at Post Carbon Institute for nearly 20 years, Richard was a pioneering voice on resilience and the energy crisis. He was the author of fourteen books, hundreds of articles, and the award-winning monthly *Museletter.*

Richard was a skilled writer and speaker who could synthesize complex issues and ideas into understandable language. His calm demeanor, sharp wit, and intense focus made difficult and daunting facts feel bearable.

Richard was a lifelong violinist and guitarist who, more recently, took up the piano. For decades, he maintained a devoted, focused daily practice and played in bands, chamber groups, duos, and orchestras throughout his life.

Beyond his public work, those who knew him personally were struck by his genuine curiosity. He was always asking questions and truly listening for the answers.  

Join us in Santa Rosa on November 15th for an afternoon of gratitude and celebration for a life so fully and generously lived. Richard’s commemoration will be held from 2:30 to 4:00 pm, with arrival starting at 2:00 pm and a social hour to follow the program.

Seating is limited. Please use the RSVP link on EverLoved to save your spot.

Where there’s a will, there’s a way.

“The Book of Will” brings to life the chaotic, hilarious, passionate, and mostly true endeavor to compile Shakespeare’s plays into the legendary First Folio!

About the show: Without William Shakespeare, we wouldn’t have literary masterpieces like “Romeo and Juliet.” But without Henry Condell and John Heminges, we would have lost half of Shakespeare’s plays forever! After the death of their friend and mentor, the two actors are determined to compile the First Folio and preserve the words that shaped their lives. They’ll just have to borrow, beg, and band together to get it done. Amidst the noise and color of Elizabethan London, The Book of Will finds an unforgettable true story of love, loss, and laughter, and sheds new light on a man you may think you know.

Two-time Grammy-winning singer and master songwriter Jim Lauderdale is both a "songwriter's songwriter," who's written/co-written many modern classics for iconic artists, as well as an intuitive sideman, who's enhanced the music of a bevy of esteemed musicians. For several decades, Jim has written songs for and worked with some of the finest artists in traditional and modern music including Ralph Stanley, Elvis Costello, George Strait, Buddy Miller, Lucinda Williams, John Oates, Solomon Burke, Lee Ann Womack, Old Crow Medicine Show, Mary Chapin Carpenter, Blake Shelton, the Dixie Chicks, Vince Gill, Patty Loveless, and Gary Allan among others.

Whether solo or band, Jim Lauderdale a triple threat performer, songwriter and musician who is constantly reinventing himself!

Overeaters Anonymous (OA) is a fellowship of people who support each other in recovering from compulsive eating and food behaviors. If you feel you have a problem with food, OA welcomes you—no matter what your background, beliefs, or eating habits.

OA is **not** a diet club or calorie-counting program.

title: Trio da Paz
description: Grammy-nominated Trio da Paz, one of the most visible Brazilian jazz groups in the world featuring three of Brazil's most-in-demand musicians: Romero Lubambo on guitar, Nilson Matta on bass and Duduka da Fonseca on drums and percussion. They formed in 1986 and will be celebrating their 40th anniversary at THE 222 in an exclusive West Coast appearance. Together, Trio da Paz performs with a strong sense of cohesion, bringing energy, imagination, and a deep musical connection to their work. The result is a trio that continues to create distinctive, personal music, blending Brazilian traditions with elements of modern jazz. Trio da Paz's sound reflects a thoughtful integration of Brazilian musical styles and jazz improvisation, drawing on the harmonies of bossa nova, the rhythms of samba, and the melodic intricacy of choro. Their acoustic trio format-guitar, bass, and drums-allows for close interaction among the musicians, fostering a conversational approach that highlights both rhythmic interplay and harmonic nuance. While grounded in tradition, the group approaches familiar forms with flexibility, allowing the music to evolve in unexpected but natural directions. Each member, established on the New York jazz scene as both a leader and collaborator, contributes to a collective identity shaped by original compositions alongside interpretations of Brazilian repertoire.

title: Antarctica: The Frozen Desert | Photographs by Vegar Abelsnes
description:
1st Street Gallery at WTRSHD will present “Antarctica: The Frozen Desert,” a new body of fine art photography by Vegar Abelsnes, opening September 26th, 2026, and on view September through November.  The exhibition marks a deliberate turn in Abelsnes’ photography; after more than two decades of working in a commercial and advertising capacity, he has embarked on a career as a photo and field guide in the polar regions. The exhibit features work generated over 6 voyages to the Antarctic Peninsula. He is returning to Antarctica in January and will add the Falklands and South Georgia to his list of destinations to guide and photograph.

Traveling to some of the most remote and inhospitable coastlines on Earth, Abelsnes has photographed a landscape that exists almost entirely outside of human time. The ice in these images began forming millions of years ago, while Homo sapiens have only existed for roughly 300,000 years. Defined by such a scale, Antarctica is less a place than a record — vast, indifferent, treacherous, and staggeringly beautiful, holding a kind of cosmic truth that Abelsnes says is more important now than ever before.

Fundamental practices for understanding the holistic nature, energetics and Sanskrit yoga philosophy guiding the approach of this comprehensive system. Long time yoga practitioners as well as new students will benefit. Experience the distinction of this system verses other modern yoga/vinyasa practices commonly taught & the traditional & precise use of ujjayi breath as it relates to the Sanskrit parameters, moving with the breath and the importance of the pause. Talasana is a very unique & profound krama initiating & establishing "samasthiti", the steadiness and focus of mind, balanced energy and steadiness of body - with the two feet together, moving from the center, all the major joints and muscles of the body are exercised using arm and hand movements, back bends, side bends, twists, forward bends, squats and balancing foot stretches. The fingers interlaced create a prana circuit as they come together in the repetitive movement over the head. The breath specific movements stretch the diaphragm, psoas, massage the heart and internal organs, clear the lungs, drain the lymphatic system, stimulate the vagus nerve and calm the mind. Energy is created along the spine and central nervous system, and is distributed throughout the nadis and into the entire energy body. Regular practice of Talasana flowers into to ananta samapatti and understanding "stillness in movement".
Class begins with Opening Mantras & Ding Namaskar (Devotional Salutation to the Directional Spheres with Breath & Mantra). Then moves to Tāĺāsana to Savasana then Seated Prānāyāma (Yogic Breathing) including Morning Cleansing Kriyas, Ujjayi, Nadi Shuddi, Samantraka Prānāyāma, Pratyahara, Dharana. title: EAMES & EAMES: Meet the couple who Defined Modern Design
location: The MAC - Napa Valley Museum of Art & Culture
description:
EAMES & EAMES: Meet the couple who Defined Modern Design

Created in collaboration with the Eames Institute of Infinite Curiosity.

EAMES & EAMES explores the iterative, hands-on, and human-centered approach of Charles & Ray Eames. Through furniture, toys, paintings, graphics, and personal belongings collected over their lifetimes, this groundbreaking exhibition looks beyond the iconic Eames chairs to reveal the breadth of their creative practice. More than any single object, their work opened doors to new and unexpected ways of seeing, thinking, making, and understanding the world—ideas that continue to inspire us today.

Curated by Llisa Demetrios, Co-Founder & The Lucia Eames Chief Curator of the Eames Institute of Infinite Curiosity.

title: Maple Magic & Winter Wonder

Maple Magic & Winter Wonder invites visitors to experience this special time of year through nature, creativity, and connection. Throughout the season, the Garden offers guided walks, hands-on workshops, lectures, and special experiences inspired by the changing landscape. Wander among vibrant fall foliage, breathe in the sweet fragrance of katsura trees, enjoy creative programs, and experience the peaceful beauty of the Garden as it transitions into winter.

title: Art Exhibit: Aspirations
description:
Date: FOR IMMEDIATE RELEASE  9/15/26

**OCTOBER EXHIBIT: ASPIRATIONS**

EXHIBIT DATES **– September 28 – October 25, 2026**

**RECEPTION: SATURDAY, October 3, 2026, 3-6 pm: Join us to meet Laura Roney and Linda Loveland Reid and learn about their art and inspiration.  Be sure to take part in the Gallery’s free monthlong drawing for a beautiful work by a Gallery artist.  Refreshments will be served.**

Sonoma County artist, **Laura Roney,** unveils **Aspirations**, a new collection of paintings in oil, celebrating the unique differing goals people set during our lives, challenging us to take bold steps forward.  Of universal inspiration**, Aspiration and Awe** splashes the Milky Way’s starry brilliance across the heavens, capturing our imagination and hope as worldly cares are left behind.  Moving from natural forces to human endeavor, looking toward social change, **Aspiring to Vote**, the portrait of a hopeful suffragette, evokes the dream for a better future.  A lifetime goal for many, the marathon, **Aspiring for 26.2,** captures the early morning excitement waiting for start times.  “People doing ordinary things but dreaming larger for the future has been a great inspiration for this series.  I hope folks will be inspired by the boldness of people’s dreams,” commented Roney on her inspiration for the work.

Art has been a lifelong passion for Roney.  Beginning her art studies at a young age, whatever avenue she was pursuing in life, she continued her artistic endeavors.  After a successful career in microbiology and pharmaceutical research, a family move to Northern California enabled Roney to focus on her art.  She received her MFA from Academy of Art University, San Francisco.

Meet the artist: Roney will host the Gallery on September 30 and October 1 from 11am to 6 pm.

The Stairway Smallworks Showcase features Linda Loveland Reid’s **Intentional Chaos,** a collection of exciting mixed-media works that explode with excitement and energy. Random patterns, amorphous shapes and dancing dribbles magically coalesce into bold statements.  Intriguing and compelling, like interlocking gears, in **Patterns of Memory** multiple patterns interlock on fields of gold and black.  “I love throwing ink, paint and even coffee onto a blank canvas and creating through instinct, gesture and emotion.  Distilling energy into smaller works brings new challenges and some happy surprises,” noted Reid on her creative process.

Meet the artist: Reid will host the Gallery on October 23 from 11am to 6 pm.

 Also join us for **ART NITE HEALDSBURG**, Thursday, October 1, 5 – 7 pm.  ART NITE Healdsburg, held the 1st Thursday of Every Month, is a community event celebrating art and creativity with over 20 galleries participating.  ArtNiteHealdsburg.com.

For further information: Contact: Beverly Bird, Press Contact, at bvdrio@sonic.net or 707-799-1490.

title: Art Exhibit: Endless Inspiration
description:
Date: FOR IMMEDIATE RELEASE  10/12/26

**NOVEMBER EXHIBIT: ENDLESS INSPIRATION**

EXHIBIT DATES **– October 26  – November 22, 2026**

**RECEPTION: SATURDAY, November 7, 2026, 3-6 pm: Join us to meet Ron Sumner and Karen Miller and learn about their art and inspiration.  Be sure to take part in the Gallery’s free monthlong drawing for a beautiful work by a Gallery artist.  Refreshments will be served.**

Sonoma County artist, **Ron Sumner,** presents **Endless Inspiration**, a collection of new paintings and classic works that highlight his lifelong love of nature featuring landscapes, animals and wildlife, with a special focus on birds.  The essence of this golden state shines forth in “California Hills,” a large oil painting of a sweep of oak covered hills.   Turning to wildlife, Sumner’s masterful watercolor rendition in the “Young Fox” captures its wild nature on stark alert.  And the compelling presence of a most majestic bird is beautifully memorialized in his “Blue Heron” watercolor.  Other birds depicted in his works include parrots, penguins and owls.  “In my painting, I always strive to translate my emotional response to the world of nature around us – to share this deep feeling with those who view my work,” commented Sumner on his inspiration.

A lifelong Northern Californian, Sumner began his art training in school.  After earning a BFA from the California College of Arts & Crafts, he was a technical illustrator for a number of years before transitioning to a full-time fine arts painter.  With an emphasis in watercolor, he has won numerous awards, including Best of Show at the Society of Western Artists.  His portrait of John F. Kennedy is part of the permanent collection at the John F. Kennedy Library.  He has exhibited widely and was part of the Veterans Art Show for CA vets in 2023.

Meet the artist: Sumner will co-host Art Nite on 11/5 from 5 pm to 7 pm.

The Stairway Smallworks Showcase features **Karen Miller’**s **Historic Gems,** featuring pastel paintings that honor our history – local artifacts that are disappearing.  Highlighting this exhibit, “Ghost Bridge,” an early 20th century railroad bridge known as Healdsburg Railroad Bridge is soon to give way for the Smart Train.  Its unique style is a key element to our local character but sadly could not be upgraded for modern rail.  From old trucks to a beloved schoolhouse, these paintings harken fond memories.  Part of our world for years, they enriched our lives and are not to be forgotten.  Noted Miller on the impetus for her series, “I want to catch old things before they’re gone – memorializing those things close to our hearts.”

Meet the artist: Miller will host the Gallery on October 26 and November 2, 11, 14 & 15 from 11am to 2:30 pm.

 Also join us for **ART NITE HEALDSBURG**, Thursday, November 5, 5 – 7 pm.  ART NITE Healdsburg, held the 1st Thursday of Every Month, is a community event celebrating art and creativity with over 20 galleries participating.  ArtNiteHealdsburg.com.

title: Winsor & Newton Professional Watercolour Series - Class 3 of 3: Lionfish
location: Rileystreet Art Supply,103 Maxwell Ct, Santa Rosa, CA 95401, USA
description:
Instructor: Ryan Martin

Date: Monday, November 16th

Time: 12:30PM-2PM

Location: Santa Rosa Store

Free!


Class 3 of 3: Lionfish — This is number three in a series of three classes using Winsor & Newton Professional Watercolour with artist Ryan Martin. Attend all three to learn week-by-week from Ryan but none are prerequisites if your schedule does not allow. In this 90-minute session, Ryan will guide you through painting a detailed lionfish while learning how to use negative space and Art Masking Fluid to preserve bright whites and create dramatic contrast. You’ll explore expressive brush strokes, layered washes, and controlled color placement as you build the fish’s flowing fins, stripes, and patterns. Masking fluid will be used to save crisp highlights and delicate details, allowing the color and movement of the paint to shine. This class focuses on seeing shapes, protecting the white of the paper, and letting watercolour create energy, texture, and life on the surface. All supplies are provided, so you can try different pigments, colors, and brushes and discover what you enjoy using. Ryan will also be available after class to answer questions and help you choose materials to keep exploring at home.


Limited seats available—reserve your spot today!


Ryan Martin lives and works in the San Francisco Bay Area where he attended the California College of the Arts. Through painting and drawing, Martin creates surreal, dream-like compositions of his subjects. He is influenced by his Native American (Mexican/Seri) and Russian heritage through painting reinterpretations of war bonnets and kokoshniks haloing his subjects. Martin’s artwork has been highlighted by numerous media including The Advocate, Creative Boom, The Art of Man and others. He has exhibited widely across the United States, including the deYoung Museum, Mark Wolfe Contemporary, Modern Eden Gallery of San Francisco, Elizabeth Houston Gallery of NYC, as well as numerous fairs including SCOPE, Untitled Art in Miami and Volta NY.

title: Salsa Beginners 2 - Mondays
description:
Ready to take your salsa to the next level? Salsa lessons in Marin will help you to add some flair and fluidity to your salsa dancing.

Pre-requisite: Salsa Beginners 1 – You know your basic steps, left turn, right turn, cross-body lead, and you hold your frame.

What You’ll Learn

We’ve curated a curriculum designed to build your confidence and your “social dance” vocabulary:

• The Cross Body Lead \(CBL\) Series: Master both Inside and Outside Turns, the essential building blocks for moving your partner across the floor with grace.

• The “I Turn – You Turn”: A classic social dance staple that develops timing and hand-change coordination.

• The Walk-Through: Learn how to transition smoothly through the dance space without breaking your rhythm.

• Footwork & Shine: We’ll break down the footwork pattern that adds personality to your “shines.”

Technique & Artistry

• Dancing is about more than just where your feet go. In this level, we dive deeper into the “how”:

• The Frame: Understand the “tension and compression” needed to lead and follow clearly without using muscle.

• Upper Body Mechanics: Learn how to isolate your ribcage and shoulders to move with that authentic Latin soul.

• Connection: Developing a “heavy” but responsive arm connection to ensure your partner feels every lead.

Important Details

• No dance experience required: Whether you’ve never danced before or it’s been a while, you’re welcome here!

• No partner necessary: Come solo or bring a friend—either way, you’ll have plenty of opportunities to dance.

• Please wear non-marking shoe soles: This helps us keep our dance floor in great condition.

title: Antarctica: The Frozen Desert | Photographs by Vegar Abelsnes
description:
1st Street Gallery at WTRSHD will present “Antarctica: The Frozen Desert,” a new body of fine art photography by Vegar Abelsnes, opening September 26th, 2026, and on view September through November.  The exhibition marks a deliberate turn in Abelsnes’ photography; after more than two decades of working in a commercial and advertising capacity, he has embarked on a career as a photo and field guide in the polar regions. The exhibit features work generated over 6 voyages to the Antarctic Peninsula. He is returning to Antarctica in January and will add the Falklands and South Georgia to his list of destinations to guide and photograph.

Traveling to some of the most remote and inhospitable coastlines on Earth, Abelsnes has photographed a landscape that exists almost entirely outside of human time. The ice in these images began forming millions of years ago, while Homo sapiens have only existed for roughly 300,000 years. Defined by such a scale, Antarctica is less a place than a record — vast, indifferent, treacherous, and staggeringly beautiful, holding a kind of cosmic truth that Abelsnes says is more important now than ever before.

location: The MAC - Napa Valley Museum of Art & Culture
description:
EAMES & EAMES: Meet the couple who Defined Modern Design

Created in collaboration with the Eames Institute of Infinite Curiosity.

EAMES & EAMES explores the iterative, hands-on, and human-centered approach of Charles & Ray Eames. Through furniture, toys, paintings, graphics, and personal belongings collected over their lifetimes, this groundbreaking exhibition looks beyond the iconic Eames chairs to reveal the breadth of their creative practice. More than any single object, their work opened doors to new and unexpected ways of seeing, thinking, making, and understanding the world—ideas that continue to inspire us today.

Curated by Llisa Demetrios, Co-Founder & The Lucia Eames Chief Curator of the Eames Institute of Infinite Curiosity.

title: Art Exhibit: Aspirations
description:
Date: FOR IMMEDIATE RELEASE  9/15/26

**OCTOBER EXHIBIT: ASPIRATIONS**

EXHIBIT DATES **– September 28 – October 25, 2026**

**RECEPTION: SATURDAY, October 3, 2026, 3-6 pm: Join us to meet Laura Roney and Linda Loveland Reid and learn about their art and inspiration.  Be sure to take part in the Gallery’s free monthlong drawing for a beautiful work by a Gallery artist.  Refreshments will be served.**

Sonoma County artist, **Laura Roney,** unveils **Aspirations**, a new collection of paintings in oil, celebrating the unique differing goals people set during our lives, challenging us to take bold steps forward.  Of universal inspiration**, Aspiration and Awe** splashes the Milky Way’s starry brilliance across the heavens, capturing our imagination and hope as worldly cares are left behind.  Moving from natural forces to human endeavor, looking toward social change, **Aspiring to Vote**, the portrait of a hopeful suffragette, evokes the dream for a better future.  A lifetime goal for many, the marathon, **Aspiring for 26.2,** captures the early morning excitement waiting for start times.  “People doing ordinary things but dreaming larger for the future has been a great inspiration for this series.  I hope folks will be inspired by the boldness of people’s dreams,” commented Roney on her inspiration for the work.

Art has been a lifelong passion for Roney.  Beginning her art studies at a young age, whatever avenue she was pursuing in life, she continued her artistic endeavors.  After a successful career in microbiology and pharmaceutical research, a family move to Northern California enabled Roney to focus on her art.  She received her MFA from Academy of Art University, San Francisco.

Meet the artist: Roney will host the Gallery on September 30 and October 1 from 11am to 6 pm.

The Stairway Smallworks Showcase features Linda Loveland Reid’s **Intentional Chaos,** a collection of exciting mixed-media works that explode with excitement and energy. Random patterns, amorphous shapes and dancing dribbles magically coalesce into bold statements.  Intriguing and compelling, like interlocking gears, in **Patterns of Memory** multiple patterns interlock on fields of gold and black.  “I love throwing ink, paint and even coffee onto a blank canvas and creating through instinct, gesture and emotion.  Distilling energy into smaller works brings new challenges and some happy surprises,” noted Reid on her creative process.

Meet the artist: Reid will host the Gallery on October 23 from 11am to 6 pm.

 Also join us for **ART NITE HEALDSBURG**, Thursday, October 1, 5 – 7 pm.  ART NITE Healdsburg, held the 1st Thursday of Every Month, is a community event celebrating art and creativity with over 20 galleries participating.  ArtNiteHealdsburg.com.

Upstairs Art Gallery, 306 Center Street, Healdsburg, CA 95448. (707) 431-4214.: OPEN DAILY: 11am – 6 pm.    **www.upstairsart gallery.net** 

For further information: Contact: Beverly Bird, Press Contact, at bvdrio@sonic.net or 707-799-1490.

title: Art Exhibit: Endless Inspiration
description:
Date: FOR IMMEDIATE RELEASE  10/12/26

**NOVEMBER EXHIBIT: ENDLESS INSPIRATION**

EXHIBIT DATES **– October 26  – November 22, 2026**

**RECEPTION: SATURDAY, November 7, 2026, 3-6 pm: Join us to meet Ron Sumner and Karen Miller and learn about their art and inspiration.  Be sure to take part in the Gallery’s free monthlong drawing for a beautiful work by a Gallery artist.  Refreshments will be served.**

Sonoma County artist, **Ron Sumner,** presents **Endless Inspiration**, a collection of new paintings and classic works that highlight his lifelong love of nature featuring landscapes, animals and wildlife, with a special focus on birds.  The essence of this golden state shines forth in “California Hills,” a large oil painting of a sweep of oak covered hills.   Turning to wildlife, Sumner’s masterful watercolor rendition in the “Young Fox” captures its wild nature on stark alert.  And the compelling presence of a most majestic bird is beautifully memorialized in his “Blue Heron” watercolor.  Other birds depicted in his works include parrots, penguins and owls.  “In my painting, I always strive to translate my emotional response to the world of nature around us – to share this deep feeling with those who view my work,” commented Sumner on his inspiration.

A lifelong Northern Californian, Sumner began his art training in school.  After earning a BFA from the California College of Arts & Crafts, he was a technical illustrator for a number of years before transitioning to a full-time fine arts painter.  With an emphasis in watercolor, he has won numerous awards, including Best of Show at the Society of Western Artists.  His portrait of John F. Kennedy is part of the permanent collection at the John F. Kennedy Library.  He has exhibited widely and was part of the Veterans Art Show for CA vets in 2023.

Meet the artist: Sumner will co-host Art Nite on 11/5 from 5 pm to 7 pm.

The Stairway Smallworks Showcase features **Karen Miller’**s **Historic Gems,** featuring pastel paintings that honor our history – local artifacts that are disappearing.  Highlighting this exhibit, “Ghost Bridge,” an early 20th century railroad bridge known as Healdsburg Railroad Bridge is soon to give way for the Smart Train.  Its unique style is a key element to our local character but sadly could not be upgraded for modern rail.  From old trucks to a beloved schoolhouse, these paintings harken fond memories.  Part of our world for years, they enriched our lives and are not to be forgotten.  Noted Miller on the impetus for her series, “I want to catch old things before they’re gone – memorializing those things close to our hearts.”

Meet the artist: Miller will host the Gallery on October 26 and November 2, 11, 14 & 15 from 11am to 2:30 pm.

 Also join us for **ART NITE HEALDSBURG**, Thursday, November 5, 5 – 7 pm.  ART NITE Healdsburg, held the 1st Thursday of Every Month, is a community event celebrating art and creativity with over 20 galleries participating.  ArtNiteHealdsburg.com.

For further information: Contact: Beverly Bird, Press Contact, at bvdrio@sonic.net or 707-799-1490.

title: The Kabbalah of Meaning
description:
Jewish Wisdom for a Life That Matters

No matter how much we achieve, something within us still asks: “Is this it? Isn’t there something more?”

The Kabbalah of Meaning is a new six-session JLI course exploring the Jewish answer to that question. What are we really searching for—and where can it be found?

Drawing on Kabbalah and centuries of Jewish wisdom, we’ll uncover the essential building blocks of a deeply meaningful life. We’ll explore how purpose can be found in our work, relationships, challenges, accomplishments, and even the ordinary routines that fill our days.

You don’t have to revamp your life. You don’t need to meditate on a mountaintop. You simply need a new lens through which to see the rich world of meaning already woven into every part of your life.

Thoughtful, practical, and surprisingly relevant, this course offers fresh perspectives and useful tools for living with greater clarity, connection, and intention.

Try 1st class free.

No previous Jewish learning required. Come as you are—and bring your questions.

title: Intermediate Salsa Class
description:
This class is designed for dancers who have a solid grasp of the basics and are eager to expand their repertoire with more complex and fluid movements.

Pre- requisite:

Salsa Class Beginners

Each week, we’ll break down a new move, focusing on the technique and connection that will make you a more confident and stylish dancer. We’ll go beyond the foundational steps to cover a wide range of essential intermediate patterns and styling, including:

Turns and Spins:

Master your inside and outside turns, double spins, and the elegant 360 and Hand Toss moves.

Intricate Patterns:

Learn to execute the 360, wrap, as well as various Cross Body Lead variations like the U-Turn and Spiral.

Footwork and Styling:

Enhance your rhythm and flair with advanced footwork like the Suzy Q, Front Tap, and Mambo Step. We’ll also work on styling with a wrap and improving your posture and upper body movement.

This class is your chance to refine your technique, improve your lead-follow connection, and add a variety of fun and dynamic moves to your salsa vocabulary. Join us and elevate your dance!

title: The Santa Rosa Original Certified Farmers Market
location: Luther Burbank Center for the Arts
description: The Santa Rosa Original Certified Farmers Market is a year-round Saturday tradition in Sonoma County, bringing together local farmers, ranchers, food artisans, and neighbors from 8:30 a.m. to 1 p.m. This is not just a place to shop, it's a place to connect directly with the people who grow your food. As a Slow Food Sonoma County award recipient, the market prioritizes integrity, seasonality, and true farm-to-community relationships. Expect peak-season produce harvested just hours before market, pasture-raised meats, fresh flowers, artisan breads, handcrafted goods, and thoughtfully prepared foods that reflect the region's agricultural richness. Visitors can stroll the vibrant open-air market, sample local flavors, and experience Sonoma County's food culture in its most authentic form. Families, chefs, and weekend explorers alike gather here to discover what's growing now and to support small farms that keep our local food system strong. Open every Saturday, rain or shine, the Santa Rosa Original Certified Farmers Market is a cornerstone of the community and a must-visit stop for anyone wanting to taste, shop, and experience Sonoma County at its freshest.

title: Antarctica: The Frozen Desert | Photographs by Vegar Abelsnes
description:
1st Street Gallery at WTRSHD will present “Antarctica: The Frozen Desert,” a new body of fine art photography by Vegar Abelsnes, opening September 26th, 2026, and on view September through November.  The exhibition marks a deliberate turn in Abelsnes’ photography; after more than two decades of working in a commercial and advertising capacity, he has embarked on a career as a photo and field guide in the polar regions. The exhibit features work generated over 6 voyages to the Antarctic Peninsula. He is returning to Antarctica in January and will add the Falklands and South Georgia to his list of destinations to guide and photograph.

Traveling to some of the most remote and inhospitable coastlines on Earth, Abelsnes has photographed a landscape that exists almost entirely outside of human time. The ice in these images began forming millions of years ago, while Homo sapiens have only existed for roughly 300,000 years. Defined by such a scale, Antarctica is less a place than a record — vast, indifferent, treacherous, and staggeringly beautiful, holding a kind of cosmic truth that Abelsnes says is more important now than ever before.

location: The MAC - Napa Valley Museum of Art & Culture
description:
EAMES & EAMES: Meet the couple who Defined Modern Design

Created in collaboration with the Eames Institute of Infinite Curiosity.

EAMES & EAMES explores the iterative, hands-on, and human-centered approach of Charles & Ray Eames. Through furniture, toys, paintings, graphics, and personal belongings collected over their lifetimes, this groundbreaking exhibition looks beyond the iconic Eames chairs to reveal the breadth of their creative practice. More than any single object, their work opened doors to new and unexpected ways of seeing, thinking, making, and understanding the world—ideas that continue to inspire us today.

Curated by Llisa Demetrios, Co-Founder & The Lucia Eames Chief Curator of the Eames Institute of Infinite Curiosity.

From the first signs of autumn in October to the brilliant display of rare Asian maples in November and the quiet beauty of early winter in December, each visit offers something new to discover. 

Maple Magic & Winter Wonder invites visitors to experience this special time of year through nature, creativity, and connection. Throughout the season, the Garden offers guided walks, hands-on workshops, lectures, and special experiences inspired by the changing landscape. Wander among vibrant fall foliage, breathe in the sweet fragrance of katsura trees, enjoy creative programs, and experience the peaceful beauty of the Garden as it transitions into winter.

title: A Taste of Italy at Centennial Mountain Tasting Room
description:
For wine drinkers eager to experience world-class wines made in California from Italian varieties, the Centennial Mountain Tasting Room is a must during any trip to Sonoma County. Located just off the plaza in the charming town of Healdsburg near famed restaurants, boutiques and galleries, the Centennial Mountain Tasting Room is a destination that invites discovery. Founded by the acclaimed team that guides renowned Pinot Noir and Chardonnay producer Rhys Vineyards, Centennial Mountain was established to explore Italian grape varieties grown on its acclaimed Centennial Mountain Vineyard in the rugged mountains of Northern Sonoma County.

The Centennial Mountain Vineyard Tasting features the winery’s coveted Nebbiolo, and the pioneering Carricante and Nerello Mascalese wines, among others. To showcase how beautifully the wines pair with food, the winery also offers a delicious Wine and Sushi Pairing from nearby Asahi Sushi, one of Healdsburg’s most popular dining destinations.

Guests can also enhance their tasting experience with a curated salumi board from Journeyman Meat Company. This generous accompaniment features six house-made salumi, crostini, cornichons, olives, and a selection of local cheese that serves 2 to 5 guests.

title: Art Exhibit: Endless Inspiration
description:
Date: FOR IMMEDIATE RELEASE  10/12/26

**NOVEMBER EXHIBIT: ENDLESS INSPIRATION**

EXHIBIT DATES **– October 26  – November 22, 2026**

**RECEPTION: SATURDAY, November 7, 2026, 3-6 pm: Join us to meet Ron Sumner and Karen Miller and learn about their art and inspiration.  Be sure to take part in the Gallery’s free monthlong drawing for a beautiful work by a Gallery artist.  Refreshments will be served.**

Sonoma County artist, **Ron Sumner,** presents **Endless Inspiration**, a collection of new paintings and classic works that highlight his lifelong love of nature featuring landscapes, animals and wildlife, with a special focus on birds.  The essence of this golden state shines forth in “California Hills,” a large oil painting of a sweep of oak covered hills.   Turning to wildlife, Sumner’s masterful watercolor rendition in the “Young Fox” captures its wild nature on stark alert.  And the compelling presence of a most majestic bird is beautifully memorialized in his “Blue Heron” watercolor.  Other birds depicted in his works include parrots, penguins and owls.  “In my painting, I always strive to translate my emotional response to the world of nature around us – to share this deep feeling with those who view my work,” commented Sumner on his inspiration.

A lifelong Northern Californian, Sumner began his art training in school.  After earning a BFA from the California College of Arts & Crafts, he was a technical illustrator for a number of years before transitioning to a full-time fine arts painter.  With an emphasis in watercolor, he has won numerous awards, including Best of Show at the Society of Western Artists.  His portrait of John F. Kennedy is part of the permanent collection at the John F. Kennedy Library.  He has exhibited widely and was part of the Veterans Art Show for CA vets in 2023.

Meet the artist: Sumner will co-host Art Nite on 11/5 from 5 pm to 7 pm.

The Stairway Smallworks Showcase features **Karen Miller’**s **Historic Gems,** featuring pastel paintings that honor our history – local artifacts that are disappearing.  Highlighting this exhibit, “Ghost Bridge,” an early 20th century railroad bridge known as Healdsburg Railroad Bridge is soon to give way for the Smart Train.  Its unique style is a key element to our local character but sadly could not be upgraded for modern rail.  From old trucks to a beloved schoolhouse, these paintings harken fond memories.  Part of our world for years, they enriched our lives and are not to be forgotten.  Noted Miller on the impetus for her series, “I want to catch old things before they’re gone – memorializing those things close to our hearts.”

Meet the artist: Miller will host the Gallery on October 26 and November 2, 11, 14 & 15 from 11am to 2:30 pm.

 Also join us for **ART NITE HEALDSBURG**, Thursday, November 5, 5 – 7 pm.  ART NITE Healdsburg, held the 1st Thursday of Every Month, is a community event celebrating art and creativity with over 20 galleries participating.  ArtNiteHealdsburg.com.

Upstairs Art Gallery, 306 Center Street, Healdsburg, CA 95448. (707) 431-4214.: OPEN DAILY: 11am – 6 pm.    **www.upstairsart gallery.net** 

For further information: Contact: Beverly Bird, Press Contact, at bvdrio@sonic.net or 707-799-1490.

title: Gratitude November Sound Healing with Bob & Amelia
description:
ratitude November Sound Healing

with Bob & Amelia

Wednesday, November 18th, 2026 • 5:30pm to 7:15pm Flatbed Farm with AB Creations 10% proceeds Cancer Support Sonoma Pouring partner Lexi Loose Leaf Tea

Step into a season of thanks at FlatBed Farm for a heartfelt evening of sound healing, reflection, and gratitude. As the year winds down, we invite you to pause, breathe, and honor the people, moments, and blessings that fill your life. Let's give thanks together!

As golden light settles over the fields, gather in community at FlatBed Farm, an intimate sanctuary nestled in the heart of wine country overlooking Sonoma Regional Park. Lying down cozy in your space in the barn, allow the soothing vibrations of crystal singing bowls, gentle percussion, and melodic chimes to wash over you, opening your heart and harmonizing mind, body, and spirit. This makes a great evening with friends or a date night!

Bob & Amelia's sound healing experience is like no other. The evening begins at 5:30 pm with time to settle into the beauty of the farm, followed by the sound healing journey from 5:45–6:45 pm. Afterwards, linger and connect over a farm-fresh Lexi loose leaf tea during a gratitude journaling and ceremonial community closing toast.

This evening gives back, too. Ten percent of proceeds benefit Cancer Support Sonoma, a local nonprofit offering affordable integrative therapies that ease the physical, mental, and emotional effects of cancer treatment for our Sonoma Valley neighbors. Don't miss this evening of gratitude and giving at FlatBed Farm, a sanctuary for renewal, connection, and heartfelt thanks. Reserve your spot now. All three sold out last year, and we love our community!

description: The Rainbow Book Club is cohosted by Mindy from Napa County Library and Napa Bookmine staff members Kass and Jules. The book club focuses on books that explore and embrace queer identity. This is a free event, but we appreciate your RSVP so we can plan for your attendance! We look forward to welcoming you. ABOUT THE BOOK “Candy cane-coated catnip for those of us who grew up on Disney Channel Original Movies and wished they made them now for adults! Rollicking, imaginative, and sweetly steamy, The Nightmare Before Kissmas transports readers to a holiday world you won’t want to leave.” — Timothy Janovsky, author of You’re a Mean One, Matthew Prince “Things get spicy, quickly, and this book is as delightfully weird as it is funny, fluffy, and immersive in a fantasy world where problems revolve around hookups and the holidays, not well, you know what we’re dealing with here on earth.” —Vulture “An irreverent holiday fantasy that involves court politics, young-adult growing pains, and holiday cheer…equal parts silly and romantic.” —Booklist AN INSTANT USA TODAY AND INDIE BESTSELLER! Red, White & Royal Blue meets The Nightmare Before Christmas in a sexy, quirky rom-com where the golden-hearted Prince of Christmas falls for the totally off-limits Prince of Halloween. Nicholas “Coal” Claus used to love Christmas. Until his father, the reigning Santa, turned the holiday into a PR façade. Coal will do anything to escape the spectacle, including getting tangled in a drunken, supremely hot make-out session with a beautiful man behind a seedy bar one night. But the heir to Christmas is soon commanded to do his duty: he will marry his best friend, Iris, the Easter Princess and his brother’s not-so-secret crush. A situation that has disaster written all over it. Things go from bad to worse when a rival arrives to challenge Coal for the princess’s hand…and Coal comes face-to-face with his mysterious behind-the-bar hottie: Hex, the Prince of Halloween. It’s a fake competition between two holiday princes who can’t keep their hands off each other over a marriage of convenience that no one wants. And it all leads to one of the sweetest, sexiest, messiest, most delightfully unforgettable love stories of the year. ABOUT THE AUTHOR Sara Raasch is the New York Times and USA Today bestselling author of the irreverently witty, tantalizingly sexy adult romances, The Entanglement of Rival Wizards, Go Luck Yourself and Nightmare Before Kissmas. Her books have been featured in the New York Times, People, NPR, Us Weekly, Elle, Vulture, and more. She grew up among the cornfields of Ohio and currently lives in the historical corridor of southeastern Virginia.

title: California Guitar Trio
description:
The universe of guitar knows no boundaries for The California Guitar Trio. Since 1991, the group has enthralled listeners with a singular sound that fearlessly crisscrosses genres. The trio’s questing spirit drives it to explore the intersections between rock, jazz, classical, and world music. It even throws in the occasional surf or spaghetti Western tune for good measure. 

Comprised of Bert Lams, Hideyo Moriya and Paul Richards, the group has established a unique, personal connection with audiences. In addition to dazzling musicianship and interplay, The California Guitar Trio's \(CGT\) shows are full of captivating stories and humor that enable concertgoers to feel like they're part of the music, not just spectators. In fact, the group’s goal is to transcend their instruments, so people focus on the music first, and its considerable technical prowess a distant second. 

CGT's 16 albums, streamed over 65 million times on Pandora, offer diverse snapshots of the group’s mercurial muse. The trio’s most recent release Komorebi showcases its acoustic side, with beautiful lush originals and innovative cover arrangements of Beatles, Beach Boys and more. Other highlights include Masterworks and album of classical works, with expansive takes on Bach, Beethoven, Arvo Pärt, and Schubert. Andromeda, which combines their many influences into a visionary album of original material; CG3\+2, an exploration of kinetic rock territory in collaboration with bassist Tony Levin and drummer Pat Mastelotto; and Echoes, which reimagines timeless material by artists such as Mike Oldfield, Penguin Café Orchestra, Pink Floyd, and Queen. 

The trio’s output has made a major global impact, having served as the soundtrack for Olympics coverage, and programs on CNN, CBS, NBC, and ESPN. They have fans in high places too: Nasa used their music to wake the crew aboard the Space Shuttle Endeavour. 

CGT's lineup is truly the sum of its distinct parts: A Utah native now residing in Los Angeles, Paul Richards immersed himself in rock, blues, jazz, and folk during his early days and while attending The University of Utah’s jazz guitar program. Bert Lams, originally from Belgium, graduated from the prestigious Royal Conservatory of Music in Brussels, specializing in classical guitar. Tokyo-born Hideyo Moriya began his guitar journey with surf music and British rock, before relocating to Boston to study at Berklee. 

All three felt the call to push themselves to the limit by enrolling in Robert Fripp’s challenging Guitar Craft courses, where they first met in 1987. They went on to tour together as part of Fripp’s League of Crafty Guitarists, before forming the California Guitar Trio in Los Angeles four years later. 

Recently, the trio expanded its collaborative possibilities by working within a six-guitar format with the Montreal Guitar Trio. During these groundbreaking, highly-entertaining shows, the acts perform inventive arrangements of each other’s repertoire, and new music for guitar sextet. 

30 years and 1,900\+ gigs later, the CGT remains intensely committed to explore, evolve and communicate a wide-ranging musical worldview. 

- By Anil Prasad

title: Antarctica: The Frozen Desert | Photographs by Vegar Abelsnes
description:
1st Street Gallery at WTRSHD will present “Antarctica: The Frozen Desert,” a new body of fine art photography by Vegar Abelsnes, opening September 26th, 2026, and on view September through November.  The exhibition marks a deliberate turn in Abelsnes’ photography; after more than two decades of working in a commercial and advertising capacity, he has embarked on a career as a photo and field guide in the polar regions. The exhibit features work generated over 6 voyages to the Antarctic Peninsula. He is returning to Antarctica in January and will add the Falklands and South Georgia to his list of destinations to guide and photograph.

Traveling to some of the most remote and inhospitable coastlines on Earth, Abelsnes has photographed a landscape that exists almost entirely outside of human time. The ice in these images began forming millions of years ago, while Homo sapiens have only existed for roughly 300,000 years. Defined by such a scale, Antarctica is less a place than a record — vast, indifferent, treacherous, and staggeringly beautiful, holding a kind of cosmic truth that Abelsnes says is more important now than ever before.

·         Henry Edward Frank, Yurok/Kashaya Pomo, who will show paintings and work with Legos titled Mind Prison,

·         Digital artist Nicolas \(Nico\) Vargas, Kashia Band of Pomo Indians, whose art was featured at the 55th Annual Stanford Powwow.

·         plus Gloria Carretero; Rose Hammock; Rudy Hammock; Jocelyn Garcia; Arella Ortega LaRose, Kashia Band of Pomo Indians; Angelica Smith, Manchester Point Arena and Yokayo Rancheria; Maria Pasalo; Michelle Napoli; Martina Morgan, Kashia Band of Pomo Indians; Hands Lopez; Shashoni Hanover-Redenbaugh; Katie Williams-Elliott, Juan Partida, and Mia Pasalo, Big Valley Pomo Tribe.

description:
EAMES & EAMES: Meet the couple who Defined Modern Design

Created in collaboration with the Eames Institute of Infinite Curiosity.

EAMES & EAMES explores the iterative, hands-on, and human-centered approach of Charles & Ray Eames. Through furniture, toys, paintings, graphics, and personal belongings collected over their lifetimes, this groundbreaking exhibition looks beyond the iconic Eames chairs to reveal the breadth of their creative practice. More than any single object, their work opened doors to new and unexpected ways of seeing, thinking, making, and understanding the world—ideas that continue to inspire us today.

Curated by Llisa Demetrios, Co-Founder & The Lucia Eames Chief Curator of the Eames Institute of Infinite Curiosity.

Maple Magic & Winter Wonder invites visitors to experience this special time of year through nature, creativity, and connection. title: A Taste of Italy at Centennial Mountain Tasting Room
description:
For wine drinkers eager to experience world-class wines made in California from Italian varieties, the Centennial Mountain Tasting Room is a must during any trip to Sonoma County. Located just off the plaza in the charming town of Healdsburg near famed restaurants, boutiques and galleries, the Centennial Mountain Tasting Room is a destination that invites discovery. Founded by the acclaimed team that guides renowned Pinot Noir and Chardonnay producer Rhys Vineyards, Centennial Mountain was established to explore Italian grape varieties grown on its acclaimed Centennial Mountain Vineyard in the rugged mountains of Northern Sonoma County.

The Centennial Mountain Vineyard Tasting features the winery’s coveted Nebbiolo, and the pioneering Carricante and Nerello Mascalese wines, among others. To showcase how beautifully the wines pair with food, the winery also offers a delicious Wine and Sushi Pairing from nearby Asahi Sushi, one of Healdsburg’s most popular dining destinations.

Guests can also enhance their tasting experience with a curated salumi board from Journeyman Meat Company. This generous accompaniment features six house-made salumi, crostini, cornichons, olives, and a selection of local cheese that serves 2 to 5 guests.

title: Art Exhibit: Endless Inspiration
description:
Date: FOR IMMEDIATE RELEASE  10/12/26

**NOVEMBER EXHIBIT: ENDLESS INSPIRATION**

EXHIBIT DATES **– October 26  – November 22, 2026**

**RECEPTION: SATURDAY, November 7, 2026, 3-6 pm: Join us to meet Ron Sumner and Karen Miller and learn about their art and inspiration.  Be sure to take part in the Gallery’s free monthlong drawing for a beautiful work by a Gallery artist.  Refreshments will be served.**

Sonoma County artist, **Ron Sumner,** presents **Endless Inspiration**, a collection of new paintings and classic works that highlight his lifelong love of nature featuring landscapes, animals and wildlife, with a special focus on birds.  The essence of this golden state shines forth in “California Hills,” a large oil painting of a sweep of oak covered hills.   Turning to wildlife, Sumner’s masterful watercolor rendition in the “Young Fox” captures its wild nature on stark alert.  And the compelling presence of a most majestic bird is beautifully memorialized in his “Blue Heron” watercolor.  Other birds depicted in his works include parrots, penguins and owls.  “In my painting, I always strive to translate my emotional response to the world of nature around us – to share this deep feeling with those who view my work,” commented Sumner on his inspiration.

A lifelong Northern Californian, Sumner began his art training in school.  After earning a BFA from the California College of Arts & Crafts, he was a technical illustrator for a number of years before transitioning to a full-time fine arts painter.  With an emphasis in watercolor, he has won numerous awards, including Best of Show at the Society of Western Artists.  His portrait of John F. Kennedy is part of the permanent collection at the John F. Kennedy Library.  He has exhibited widely and was part of the Veterans Art Show for CA vets in 2023.

Meet the artist: Sumner will co-host Art Nite on 11/5 from 5 pm to 7 pm.

The Stairway Smallworks Showcase features **Karen Miller’**s **Historic Gems,** featuring pastel paintings that honor our history – local artifacts that are disappearing.  Highlighting this exhibit, “Ghost Bridge,” an early 20th century railroad bridge known as Healdsburg Railroad Bridge is soon to give way for the Smart Train.  Its unique style is a key element to our local character but sadly could not be upgraded for modern rail.  From old trucks to a beloved schoolhouse, these paintings harken fond memories.  Part of our world for years, they enriched our lives and are not to be forgotten.  Noted Miller on the impetus for her series, “I want to catch old things before they’re gone – memorializing those things close to our hearts.”

Meet the artist: Miller will host the Gallery on October 26 and November 2, 11, 14 & 15 from 11am to 2:30 pm.

 Also join us for **ART NITE HEALDSBURG**, Thursday, November 5, 5 – 7 pm.  ART NITE Healdsburg, held the 1st Thursday of Every Month, is a community event celebrating art and creativity with over 20 galleries participating.  ArtNiteHealdsburg.com.

Upstairs Art Gallery, 306 Center Street, Healdsburg, CA 95448. (707) 431-4214.: OPEN DAILY: 11am – 6 pm.    **www.upstairsart gallery.net** 

For further information: Contact: Beverly Bird, Press Contact, at bvdrio@sonic.net or 707-799-1490.

description:
Instructor: Juanita Watkins
Thursdays, Ongoing
4:30PM-5:30PM
Location: Santa Rosa Location
Free!



Get HANDS-ON with local artist and calligrapher Juanita Watkins as she demonstrates the expressive power of Pilot Parallel Pens.

This fun, beginner oriented demonstration will help you discover the connection between doodling and calligraphy. Juanita will show how creating simple repetitive shapes can transform into beautiful calligraphy.

Experiment with multicolored lettering, explore shimmering gold effects with Finetec colors, and learn how to push your tools further—like using a Parallel Pen with a pointed dip pen for fine detail work and other effects.

Along the way, Juanita will cover ink behavior, alternative ink options, cleaning techniques for Parallel Pens, and introduce you to Cadel lettering.

Did we mention that this is hands on and free? Sign up soon!

title: Belly Dancing with Raja - Thursdays
description:
DATE AND TIME: Thursdays, 5:30 PM

Unlock your inner strength and find your flow. Belly dancing with Raja is an innovative fusion class that blends the rhythmic artistry of belly dance with the high-energy benefits of aerobics. Designed to be both a cardiovascular challenge and a deep toning session, this class focuses on the “powerhouse” of the body—your core.

By layering fluid, isolative movements over an athletic aerobic base, you will challenge your muscles in ways traditional gym workouts can’t reach.

What to Expect in Belly Dancing Class

• Core-Centric Power: Use undulations and shimmies to engage deep abdominal muscles for a tighter, stronger midsection.

• Functional Stability: Improve your balance and posture through controlled, hip-driven movements and low-impact aerobic footwork.

• Total Body Toning: Build lean muscle in your legs, glutes, and arms while maintaining a constant, heart-pumping pace.

• Mind-Body Connection: Enhance your coordination and body awareness through rhythmic, expressive choreography.

“Whether you’re looking to define your waistline or simply want a workout that feels like a celebration, this class offers the perfect balance of sweat and grace.”

Difficulty Level: All levels welcome! No prior dance experience is required—just bring your energy and a willingness to move.

title: THIRSTY THURSDAY New Member Social for Sonoma County Women's Wine Club
description:
Sonoma County Women's Wine Club (SCWWC)
This is our regular club meeting, held on the last Thursday of every month except for holidays and we are super excited! Come join us at 4th Street Cellars in downtown Santa Rosa. They have generously offered to host our monthly THIRSTY THURSDAY social for us.

If you are new to the area, or just looking to get out of the house and make new friends, this is the place for you. Welcoming to ALL new and (ahem, old) members.

Wine is purchased by the glass for a set fee of $13/$14 per glass with the variety of white, rosé, and red wines offered through 4th Street Cellars which includes tip. Fees are collected at the venue by Co-organizer Daima Phipps via cash, Venmo, or Paypal. You are welcome to purchase wine separately if you choose. Starting March 2025, we ask that every attending member pay a $1 "slush" fund fee per event so that we can build up our funds for club-related expenses, which can be paid by Venmo or cash.

There is no food offered, but you are welcome to bring an appetizer or snack to share with the group, and many ladies do. We will have time to socialize while tasting in the room upstairs to the left or the outside patio if the weather is nice.

The space has a 25 person attendee limit, but the list is open to 40 to eliminate a waitlist, and guests are welcome! Please RSVP below only if you are able to make it, we have an attendance policy: if you No-Show to three events, you may not attend events for the next three months. Please put this event in your calendar so you don't miss out or get dinged. A No-Show is when you are on the 'Going' list, but do not show up.

See you there, ready to kickoff!
